_meta.purpose: Evidence registry — every source logged once, referenced by id from card.src[].
_meta.status: Backfilled: every card links to a fetch-verified, openable source URL with a concrete strength note.

schema.strength: describes how THICK the evidence is, concretely (e.g. 'two RCTs, n≈12k'; 'single case study') — never a bare 'strong'/'weak'
schema.kind: book | paper | dataset | report | reference | news

ev-date-constantinople-1453.title: Fall of Constantinople
ev-date-constantinople-1453.strength: Encyclopaedic account citing contemporary chronicles; date and outcome firmly attested.

ev-date-french-revolution-1789.title: Storming of the Bastille
ev-date-french-revolution-1789.strength: Encyclopaedic account of a precisely dated, well-documented event.

ev-date-moon-landing-1969.title: Apollo 11
ev-date-moon-landing-1969.strength: NASA's official mission record — a primary source.

ev-date-hijra-622.title: Hijrah
ev-date-hijra-622.strength: Encyclopaedic account; the year anchors the Islamic calendar, the exact day is reconstructed.

ev-date-prc-1949.title: Proclamation of the People's Republic of China
ev-date-prc-1949.strength: Encyclopaedic account of a precisely dated modern event.

ev-date-berlin-wall-1989.title: Berlin Wall
ev-date-berlin-wall-1989.strength: Encyclopaedic account; the 9 Nov 1989 opening is extensively documented.

ev-hist-printing.title: Printing press
ev-hist-printing.strength: Encyclopaedic synthesis; Gutenberg's ~1440 movable type is well established.

ev-hist-blackdeath.title: Black Death
ev-hist-blackdeath.strength: Encyclopaedic synthesis of historical records and recent DNA work; mortality estimates vary (a third or more).

ev-hist-westphalia.title: Peace of Westphalia
ev-hist-westphalia.strength: Encyclopaedic account; the 'birth of sovereignty' framing is common but debated by historians.

ev-phys-entropy.title: Second law of thermodynamics
ev-phys-entropy.strength: Established physical law; entropy increase in isolated systems is among the most robustly confirmed principles in physics.

ev-phys-uncertainty.title: Uncertainty principle
ev-phys-uncertainty.strength: Core quantum-mechanics result, repeatedly confirmed experimentally.

ev-phys-cmb.title: Cosmic microwave background
ev-phys-cmb.strength: Measured at 2.725 K by COBE/WMAP/Planck; among the strongest evidence for the Big Bang.

ev-bio-natural-selection.title: Natural selection
ev-bio-natural-selection.strength: Foundational, overwhelmingly evidenced theory of biology.

ev-bio-microbiome.title: Revised Estimates for the Number of Human and Bacteria Cells in the Body
ev-bio-microbiome.strength: Peer-reviewed estimate (PLOS Biology); ~1.3:1 bacteria:human with stated uncertainty, revising the old 10:1.

ev-eco-yellowstone.title: History of wolves in Yellowstone
ev-eco-yellowstone.strength: Reintroduction is well documented; the full trophic-cascade-to-rivers claim is debated among ecologists.

ev-eco-planetary-boundaries.title: Planetary Boundaries
ev-eco-planetary-boundaries.strength: Framework from the originating research centre; the 2023 assessment finds seven of nine boundaries transgressed.

ev-eco-haber-bosch.title: Haber process
ev-eco-haber-bosch.strength: Well-established industrial chemistry; the 'feeds about half the world' figure is a widely-cited estimate.

ev-sys-feedback.title: Feedback
ev-sys-feedback.strength: Standard systems concept: reinforcing vs balancing loops.

ev-sys-commons.title: Tragedy of the commons
ev-sys-commons.strength: Hardin's model plus Ostrom's Nobel-winning empirical rebuttal — both well documented.

ev-sys-powerlaw.title: Power law
ev-sys-powerlaw.strength: Well-established pattern (Pareto/Zipf); whether a given dataset is truly power-law is often debated case by case.

ev-eh-industrial-revolution.title: Economic Growth
ev-eh-industrial-revolution.strength: Data-rich synthesis (Maddison-based series); the post-1800 takeoff in GDP per capita is well documented.

ev-eh-enclosure.title: Enclosure
ev-eh-enclosure.strength: Encyclopaedic account; the enclosure-to-wage-labour link is well attested, though its weight is debated (Marxist vs other readings).

ev-eh-bretton-woods.title: Bretton Woods system
ev-eh-bretton-woods.strength: Well-documented monetary history; the 1971 'Nixon shock' is firmly dated.

ev-eh-great-depression.title: Great Depression
ev-eh-great-depression.strength: Extensively documented; its causes are still debated among economists.

ev-eh-neoliberal-turn.title: Neoliberalism
ev-eh-neoliberal-turn.strength: Well-documented Reagan/Thatcher-era policy shift; 'neoliberalism' as a label is itself contested.

ev-fun-octopus-hearts.title: Octopus
ev-fun-octopus-hearts.strength: Encyclopaedic; three hearts and copper-based haemocyanin (blue blood) are established zoology.

ev-fun-venus-day.title: Venus: Facts
ev-fun-venus-day.strength: NASA reference: 243-Earth-day rotation vs a 225-day orbit — a measured fact.

ev-fun-1816-no-summer.title: Year Without a Summer
ev-fun-1816-no-summer.strength: Well documented: coldest European summer on record 1766–2000, linked to the 1815 Tambora eruption.

ev-fun-honey-keeps.title: The Science Behind Honey's Eternal Shelf Life
ev-fun-honey-keeps.strength: Popular-science explainer quoting a honey scientist; the mechanism (low moisture, acidity, peroxide) is well established.

ev-date-sykes-picot-1916.title: Sykes–Picot Agreement
ev-date-sykes-picot-1916.strength: Encyclopaedic account citing the released text; the secret 1916 partition is firmly documented.

ev-date-year-of-africa-1960.title: Year of Africa
ev-date-year-of-africa-1960.strength: Encyclopaedic account; the 17 independences of 1960 are well documented.

ev-geo-thucydides.title: Thucydides Trap
ev-geo-thucydides.strength: Allison's framework; widely discussed but heavily criticised — the '12 of 16 cases led to war' claim is contested.

ev-geo-hormuz.title: Strait of Hormuz
ev-geo-hormuz.strength: Figure (~20–25% of seaborne oil) corroborated by EIA data; widely cited.

ev-geo-heartland.title: The Geographical Pivot of History
ev-geo-heartland.strength: Mackinder's original 1904 thesis — a historically influential doctrine, not an empirical law.

ev-geo-demographic.title: Demographic transition
ev-geo-demographic.strength: Well-established empirical pattern across developed countries; the stage details are debated.

ev-poli-median-voter.title: Median voter theorem
ev-poli-median-voter.strength: Formal result (Black, 1948); empirically limited — real parties don't fully converge to the centre.

ev-poli-duverger.title: Duverger's law
ev-poli-duverger.strength: Robust empirical tendency rather than an absolute rule (regional-party exceptions).

ev-poli-collective-action.title: Collective action problem
ev-poli-collective-action.strength: Well-established (Olson); explains free-riding, low turnout and under-provided public goods.

ev-game-prisoners-dilemma.title: Prisoner's Dilemma
ev-game-prisoners-dilemma.strength: Peer-reviewed SEP entry; canonical, formally analysed result.

ev-game-nash-equilibrium.title: Nash equilibrium
ev-game-nash-equilibrium.strength: Foundational game-theory concept; existence proven for finite games (Nash, 1950).

ev-game-repeated.title: Repeated game
ev-game-repeated.strength: Standard game theory; the folk theorem and Axelrod's tit-for-tat are well established.

ev-econ-comparative-advantage.title: Comparative advantage
ev-econ-comparative-advantage.strength: Ricardo's 1817 result; a core, widely-taught principle (with known real-world qualifications).

ev-econ-loss-aversion.title: Loss aversion
ev-econ-loss-aversion.strength: Prospect-theory finding, widely replicated — but the universal ~2:1 ratio is now debated.

ev-econ-what-is.title: Scarcity
ev-econ-what-is.strength: Robbins's standard definition of economics via scarce means and competing ends.

ev-econ-supply-demand.title: Supply and demand
ev-econ-supply-demand.strength: Foundational model; a deliberate simplification, not a literal account of all price-setting.

ev-econ-gdp.title: Gross domestic product
ev-econ-gdp.strength: Standard national-accounts measure; its omissions are well documented (Kuznets's own 1937 caveat).

ev-pe-what-is.title: Political economy
ev-pe-what-is.strength: Encyclopaedic overview of the field's politics-and-economics scope.

ev-pe-schools.title: Schools of economic thought
ev-pe-schools.strength: Encyclopaedic survey of rival schools — grounds the card's pluralism.

ev-pe-smith-wealth.title: The Wealth of Nations
ev-pe-smith-wealth.strength: Smith's 1776 work; the invisible-hand/self-interest reading is standard (and often oversimplified).

ev-pe-division-labour.title: Division of labour
ev-pe-division-labour.strength: Smith's pin-factory example; foundational and well documented.

ev-pe-ricardo.title: David Ricardo
ev-pe-ricardo.strength: Biography and works of the classical economist.

ev-pe-ltv.title: Labor theory of value
ev-pe-ltv.strength: Classical/Marxian theory, displaced by marginalism; its validity remains contested.

ev-pe-marginalist.title: Marginalism
ev-pe-marginalist.strength: The 1870s marginal revolution (Jevons, Menger, Walras); well documented.

ev-pe-marx-capital.title: Das Kapital
ev-pe-marx-capital.strength: Marx's Capital; influential and heavily contested.

ev-pe-historical-materialism.title: Historical materialism
ev-pe-historical-materialism.strength: Marx/Engels framework; influential in sociology, criticised for economic determinism.

ev-pe-keynes.title: The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money
ev-pe-keynes.strength: Keynes's 1936 work; the demand-deficient-slump argument is standard macro.

ev-pe-paradox-thrift.title: Paradox of thrift
ev-pe-paradox-thrift.strength: A fallacy-of-composition result; standard Keynesian point, disputed by some schools.

ev-pe-friedman.title: Monetarism
ev-pe-friedman.strength: Friedman's monetarism; influential, though the money-inflation link proved unstable after the 1980s.

ev-pe-hayek.title: The Use of Knowledge in Society
ev-pe-hayek.strength: Hayek's 1945 essay — the canonical statement of the knowledge problem.

ev-cs-halting.title: Halting problem
ev-cs-halting.strength: Turing's 1936 undecidability result — a proven theorem.

ev-stat-lln.title: Law of large numbers
ev-stat-lln.strength: Proven probability theorem; the gambler's-fallacy corollary is standard.

ev-stat-clt.title: Central limit theorem
ev-stat-clt.strength: Proven theorem under stated conditions (independence, finite variance).

ev-code-naming.title: TwoHardThings
ev-code-naming.strength: Fowler's note on the well-known 'naming things' adage (Karlton) — craft consensus, not an empirical claim.

ev-code-dry.title: Don't repeat yourself
ev-code-dry.strength: DRY principle from The Pragmatic Programmer; a widely-held craft principle.

ev-code-complexity.title: Is High Quality Software Worth the Cost?
ev-code-complexity.strength: Fowler's argument that internal quality lowers cost-of-change; reasoned craft view with some empirical support (DORA).

ev-math-godel.title: Gödel's Incompleteness Theorems
ev-math-godel.strength: Peer-reviewed SEP entry on the proven 1931 theorems.

ev-math-base-rate.title: Base rate fallacy
ev-math-base-rate.strength: Standard probability result; worked rare-disease example.

ev-philo-falsifiability.title: Falsifiability
ev-philo-falsifiability.strength: Popper's demarcation criterion; influential but contested (Kuhn, Lakatos).

ev-philo-is-ought.title: Is–ought problem
ev-philo-is-ought.strength: Hume's classic problem; widely accepted, with naturalist counter-arguments.

ev-philo-veil.title: Original position (veil of ignorance)
ev-philo-veil.strength: Rawls's thought experiment; influential, criticised by Nozick, Sandel and empirical work.

ev-logic-modus-ponens.title: Modus ponens
ev-logic-modus-ponens.strength: Standard valid inference rule (with modus tollens).

ev-china-reform-opening.title: China Overview
ev-china-reform-opening.strength: World Bank country data; the 'almost 800 million out of extreme poverty since 1978' figure is its official estimate.

ev-china-party-state.title: Chinese Communist Party
ev-china-party-state.strength: Encyclopaedic; the Party's supremacy over the state, army and courts is well documented.

ev-china-century-humiliation.title: Century of humiliation
ev-china-century-humiliation.strength: Encyclopaedic; the period is well documented and the narrative's political use by the CCP is noted.

ev-china-state-structure.title: National People's Congress
ev-china-state-structure.strength: Encyclopaedic; the congress hierarchy and the NPC's formal supremacy are well documented.

ev-china-cadre-appointment.title: Cadre system of the Chinese Communist Party
ev-china-cadre-appointment.strength: Encyclopaedic account of the nomenklatura/Organization-Department appointment system; well sourced to China-studies scholarship.

ev-china-local-elections.title: Elections in China
ev-china-local-elections.strength: Encyclopaedic; the direct-village / indirect-above structure and the 1987 Organic Law are well documented.

ev-china-whole-process-democracy.title: Whole-process people's democracy
ev-china-whole-process-democracy.strength: Documents the CCP's own concept (Xi 2019; in law 2021) and the debate around it.

ev-china-marxism.title: Socialism with Chinese characteristics
ev-china-marxism.strength: Encyclopaedic; the Marxism-Leninism lineage and 'primary stage of socialism' doctrine are well documented.

ev-china-growth-model.title: Economy of China
ev-china-growth-model.strength: Encyclopaedic with cited figures (savings ~43% of GDP, SOEs ~40%, exports ~20%); the rebalancing debate is well covered.

ev-china-hukou.title: Hukou
ev-china-hukou.strength: Encyclopaedic; the rural/urban registration and ~200–300M migrant 'floating population' are well documented.

ev-china-local-debt.title: Local government financing vehicle
ev-china-local-debt.strength: Encyclopaedic, citing IMF estimates (~$8tn LGFV debt, ≈47% of GDP, end-2023) and the land-finance mechanism.

ev-china-provinces.title: Administrative divisions of China
ev-china-provinces.strength: Encyclopaedic; the 22 provinces / 5 autonomous regions / 4 municipalities / 2 SARs structure is official and well documented.

ev-china-hu-line.title: Heihe–Tengchong Line
ev-china-hu-line.strength: Long-standing demographic regularity; ~94% east / ~6% west of the line, stable since 1935 (2015 figures).

ev-china-megaregions.title: Megalopolises in China
ev-china-megaregions.strength: Encyclopaedic list of officially-recognised city clusters with population/area figures.

ev-me-sunni-shia.title: Shia–Sunni relations
ev-me-sunni-shia.strength: Encyclopaedic; the 632 succession origin and ~85% Sunni / ~15% Shia split are well documented.

ev-me-oil-rentier.title: Rentier state
ev-me-oil-rentier.strength: Established political-economy theory; the resource-revenue-not-taxes bargain is well evidenced, though its tie to autocracy is debated (Herb).

ev-me-israel-palestine.title: Israeli–Palestinian conflict
ev-me-israel-palestine.strength: Encyclopaedic overview; core dates well documented, but framing and many facts are narrated differently by each side.

ev-me-iran-saudi.title: Iran–Saudi Arabia proxy war
ev-me-iran-saudi.strength: Encyclopaedic; the proxy rivalry and 2023 China-brokered restoration of ties are well documented.

ev-colonial-scramble-africa.title: Scramble for Africa
ev-colonial-scramble-africa.strength: Encyclopaedic; the Berlin Conference (1884–85) and the partition leaving only Ethiopia and Liberia free by 1914 are well documented.

ev-sahel-region.title: Sahel
ev-sahel-region.strength: Encyclopaedic; the geography, rapid population growth and the ~35%-of-global-terrorism-deaths (2021) figure are cited.

ev-sahel-alliance.title: Alliance of Sahel States
ev-sahel-alliance.strength: Documents the post-coup bloc, the ECOWAS exit, expulsion of Western forces and the 2024 turn to Russian contractors.

ev-africa-francafrique.title: Françafrique
ev-africa-francafrique.strength: Encyclopaedic; the CFA franc, defence pacts and intervention record are documented — 'Françafrique' is itself a critical framing.

ev-libya-collapse.title: Libyan crisis
ev-libya-collapse.strength: Encyclopaedic; Gaddafi's 2011 fall and the two civil wars / east-west split are well documented.

ev-phys-time-dilation.title: Time dilation
ev-phys-time-dilation.strength: Established relativity; confirmed by muons, the Hafele–Keating atomic-clock flights and GPS corrections.

ev-phys-heat-death.title: Heat death of the universe
ev-phys-heat-death.strength: A hypothesis that follows from the second law if expansion continues; the cosmic application is debated.

ev-phys-entanglement.title: Quantum entanglement
ev-phys-entanglement.strength: Repeatedly confirmed by Bell-test experiments (2022 Nobel); no-faster-than-light-signalling is well established.

ev-phys-dark-energy.title: Dark energy
ev-phys-dark-energy.strength: Accelerating expansion seen since 1998 (Type Ia supernovae, CMB, structure); the cause remains unknown.

ev-bio-genetic-drift.title: Genetic drift
ev-bio-genetic-drift.strength: Established population genetics; drift and Kimura's neutral theory are well evidenced.

ev-bio-microbiome-role.title: Human microbiome
ev-bio-microbiome-role.strength: Core functions (fibre fermentation, vitamins, immune training) well established; many disease links are still correlational.

ev-bio-germline-editing.title: He Jiankui affair
ev-bio-germline-editing.strength: Well-documented 2018 case (twins, condemnation, 3-year sentence) and the somatic-vs-germline distinction.

ev-eco-tipping-points.title: Tipping points in the climate system
ev-eco-tipping-points.strength: Active climate-science synthesis (IPCC-tracked); the existence of tipping elements is well supported, exact thresholds uncertain.

ev-eco-keystone-species.title: Keystone species
ev-eco-keystone-species.strength: Established ecological concept with classic experiments (sea stars, otters); the label is sometimes over-applied.

ev-eco-eutrophication.title: Eutrophication
ev-eco-eutrophication.strength: Well-established mechanism; nutrient-runoff dead zones (e.g. Gulf of Mexico) are extensively documented.

ev-sys-leverage-points.title: Twelve leverage points
ev-sys-leverage-points.strength: Influential systems-thinking heuristic from Meadows; a framework, not an empirical law.

ev-sys-ostrom.title: Elinor Ostrom
ev-sys-ostrom.strength: Nobel-winning (2009) empirical work across many real commons; principles best evidenced for bounded local resources.

ev-sys-preferential-attachment.title: Preferential attachment
ev-sys-preferential-attachment.strength: Well-studied generative mechanism for power laws; one of several routes, not the only one.

ev-poli-arrow.title: Arrow's impossibility theorem
ev-poli-arrow.strength: A proven theorem in social choice; the rated-voting exception is well noted.

ev-poli-proportional.title: Proportional representation
ev-poli-proportional.strength: Well-documented electoral systems; the representativeness-vs-governability trade-off is a tendency, not a law.

ev-philo-duhem-quine.title: Duhem–Quine thesis
ev-philo-duhem-quine.strength: Influential epistemology; confirmation holism is widely accepted, its strong 'anything goes' reading is contested.

ev-philo-naturalistic-fallacy.title: Naturalistic fallacy
ev-philo-naturalistic-fallacy.strength: Classic metaethics (Principia Ethica); the 'fallacy' label is itself debated (Frankena).

ev-philo-nozick.title: Anarchy, State, and Utopia
ev-philo-nozick.strength: Canonical libertarian reply to Rawls; entitlement theory and the minimal state are well documented, the acquisition principle widely criticised.

ev-geo-rimland.title: Rimland
ev-geo-rimland.strength: Influential geopolitical doctrine that shaped US containment; a sweeping theory, not an empirical law.

ev-geo-security-dilemma.title: Security dilemma
ev-geo-security-dilemma.strength: Core IR concept, well theorised; defensive vs offensive realists debate how escapable it is.

ev-geo-malacca.title: Strait of Malacca
ev-geo-malacca.strength: Well documented: ~80% of China's crude imports transit it; 'Malacca dilemma' is Hu Jintao's 2003 framing.

ev-geo-population-decline.title: Population decline
ev-geo-population-decline.strength: Well-documented sub-replacement fertility trends (global ~2.2, S. Korea ~0.7); long-range projections are uncertain.

ev-logic-connectives.title: Logical connective
ev-logic-connectives.strength: Standard reference defining the truth-functional connectives.

ev-logic-truth-tables.title: Truth table
ev-logic-truth-tables.strength: Standard reference; truth tables are a definitional tool, not an empirical claim.

ev-logic-demorgan.title: De Morgan's laws
ev-logic-demorgan.strength: Proven logical equivalences, foundational to Boolean algebra.

ev-logic-disjunctive-syllogism.title: Disjunctive syllogism
ev-logic-disjunctive-syllogism.strength: Valid rule of inference in classical and intuitionistic logic.

ev-logic-hypothetical-syllogism.title: Hypothetical syllogism
ev-logic-hypothetical-syllogism.strength: Valid in classical logic; fails in some non-monotonic/probabilistic systems.

ev-logic-denying-antecedent.title: Denying the antecedent
ev-logic-denying-antecedent.strength: Standard formal-fallacy reference; valid only if the conditional is a biconditional.

ev-logic-quantifiers.title: Quantifier (logic)
ev-logic-quantifiers.strength: Standard first-order-logic reference (∀/∃, domains, quantifier order).

ev-logic-counterexample.title: Counterexample
ev-logic-counterexample.strength: Standard reference; one counterexample disproves a universal (a logical fact).

ev-logic-syllogism.title: Syllogism
ev-logic-syllogism.strength: Classical logic reference; Aristotle's valid forms catalogued.

ev-logic-proof-contradiction.title: Proof by contradiction
ev-logic-proof-contradiction.strength: Standard proof method; classically valid, restricted in intuitionistic logic.

ev-logic-induction.title: Mathematical induction
ev-logic-induction.strength: Rigorous proof method over the natural numbers.

ev-logic-informal-fallacies.title: Fallacy
ev-logic-informal-fallacies.strength: Standard reference; formal/informal distinction and the 'fallacy fallacy' are well covered.

ev-logic-straw-man.title: Straw man
ev-logic-straw-man.strength: Standard informal-fallacy reference; notes steelmanning as the honest opposite.

ev-logic-ad-hominem.title: Ad hominem
ev-logic-ad-hominem.strength: Standard reference; notes it's not mere insult and can be legitimate for credibility.

ev-logic-false-dilemma.title: False dilemma
ev-logic-false-dilemma.strength: Standard reference; distinguishes genuine from false binaries.

ev-logic-slippery-slope.title: Slippery slope
ev-logic-slippery-slope.strength: Standard reference; fallacious only when the causal chain is asserted, not shown.

ev-logic-begging-the-question.title: Begging the question
ev-logic-begging-the-question.strength: Standard reference; the circular-reasoning sense, distinct from 'raises the question'.

ev-logic-equivocation.title: Equivocation
ev-logic-equivocation.strength: Standard reference; the fallacy is the illegitimate meaning-shift, not ambiguity itself.

ev-logic-appeal-authority.title: Argument from authority
ev-logic-appeal-authority.strength: Standard reference; distinguishes legitimate expert consensus from misplaced authority.

ev-chang-ladder.title: Kicking Away the Ladder
ev-chang-ladder.strength: Influential heterodox argument that development came from state intervention/industrial policy, not free markets.

ev-beijing-consensus.title: Beijing Consensus
ev-beijing-consensus.strength: Frames China’s state-led model explicitly against the market-liberal Washington Consensus.

ev-rodney-underdeveloped.title: How Europe Underdeveloped Africa
ev-rodney-underdeveloped.strength: Foundational dependency-theory text arguing colonial extraction caused African underdevelopment.

ev-math-variable.title: Prealgebra 2e — 2.1 Use the Language of Algebra
ev-math-variable.strength: Peer-reviewed open textbook (Rice University/OpenStax); the standard introductory treatment of variables and algebraic expressions. Expository, not a research claim — the right kind of source for a settled definition.

ev-math-equation-balance.title: Paul's Online Notes — Algebra: Linear Equations
ev-math-equation-balance.strength: Widely used free university lecture notes; lays out the 'do the same to both sides' procedure step by step. Expository teaching reference for a settled method, not a primary source.

ev-math-function.title: Paul's Online Notes — Algebra: The Definition of a Function
ev-math-function.strength: Standard definition of a function (exactly one output per input) with worked examples; established free university notes. Definitional, not contested.

ev-math-powers.title: Paul's Online Notes — Algebra: Integer Exponents
ev-math-powers.strength: Covers exponent rules including a^m·a^n=a^(m+n) with proofs and examples; standard expository notes. The laws are settled algebra.

ev-math-log.title: Paul's Online Notes — Algebra: Logarithm Functions
ev-math-log.strength: Defines logs as inverses of exponentials and derives log(xy)=log x+log y; established free university notes. Definitional content.

ev-math-linear-equation.title: Paul's Online Notes — Algebra: Lines
ev-math-linear-equation.strength: Derives slope and the slope-intercept form y=mx+b with worked graphs; standard expository notes for settled material.

ev-math-quadratic.title: Paul's Online Notes — Algebra: Parabolas
ev-math-quadratic.strength: Treats y=ax^2+bx+c, the parabola's shape and the role of a, b, c; established free notes. The quadratic formula it relies on is a proven identity.

ev-math-summation.title: Paul's Online Notes — Calculus I: Summation Notation
ev-math-summation.strength: Defines sigma notation and its index conventions with examples; standard expository notes. Pure notation, not contested.

ev-math-limit.title: Paul's Online Notes — Calculus I: The Limit
ev-math-limit.strength: Builds the intuitive notion of a limit, including the sin(x)/x example, before the formal definition; established free university notes.

ev-math-derivative.title: Paul's Online Notes — Calculus I: The Definition of the Derivative
ev-math-derivative.strength: Defines the derivative as the limit of the difference quotient (slope of the tangent) and computes f(x)=x^2 → 2x; standard, proven calculus.

ev-math-integral.title: Paul's Online Notes — Calculus I: Definition of the Definite Integral
ev-math-integral.strength: Defines the definite integral as the limit of Riemann sums (area under a curve) and states the fundamental theorem link; established notes, settled content.

ev-math-chain-rule.title: Paul's Online Notes — Calculus I: Chain Rule
ev-math-chain-rule.strength: States and applies the chain rule d/dx f(g(x))=f'(g(x))g'(x) with worked examples; a proven theorem, expository source.

ev-math-gradient.title: Paul's Online Notes — Calculus III: Directional Derivatives
ev-math-gradient.strength: Defines the gradient as the vector of partial derivatives and proves it points in the direction of steepest increase; standard multivariable-calculus notes.

ev-la-vector.title: Essence of Linear Algebra — Vectors
ev-la-vector.strength: Widely cited visual lesson establishing the arrow/list duality of vectors; expository (teaching), but a well-regarded canonical explainer for the geometric view.

ev-la-vector-add.title: Essence of Linear Algebra — Linear combinations, span, and basis vectors
ev-la-vector-add.strength: Visual treatment of vector addition, scaling and linear combinations; canonical explainer, expository rather than primary.

ev-la-dot-product.title: Essence of Linear Algebra — Dot products and duality
ev-la-dot-product.strength: Explains a·b = Σaᵢbᵢ = |a||b|cosθ and the alignment interpretation; well-known explainer. The identity itself is a proven theorem.

ev-la-norm.title: Interactive Linear Algebra — Dot Products and Orthogonality
ev-la-norm.strength: Open Georgia Tech textbook chapter defining vector length/norm via the dot product and Euclidean distance; standard, proven definitions.

ev-la-matrix.title: Interactive Linear Algebra — Matrix Equations
ev-la-matrix.strength: Open Georgia Tech textbook chapter introducing matrices and the matrix-vector product Ax as a combination of columns; established definitional content.

ev-la-matrix-vector.title: Essence of Linear Algebra — Linear transformations and matrices
ev-la-matrix-vector.strength: Canonical visual explanation that a matrix is a linear transformation whose columns are where the basis vectors land; expository explainer of settled theory.

ev-la-matrix-mult.title: Essence of Linear Algebra — Matrix multiplication as composition
ev-la-matrix-mult.strength: Shows (AB)x = A(Bx) — multiplication as composing transformations — and why order matters; well-known explainer of a proven property.

ev-la-identity-inverse.title: Interactive Linear Algebra — Matrix Inverses
ev-la-identity-inverse.strength: Open Georgia Tech textbook chapter defining the identity, the inverse (AA⁻¹=I) and when an inverse exists; standard proven results.

ev-la-linear-system.title: Essence of Linear Algebra — Inverse matrices, column space and null space
ev-la-linear-system.strength: Frames Ax=b geometrically and explains solving via the inverse, and when no/many solutions exist; canonical explainer of settled theory.

ev-la-determinant.title: Essence of Linear Algebra — The determinant
ev-la-determinant.strength: Explains det as the area/volume scaling factor and det=0 as collapse of a dimension; well-known explainer. The ad−bc formula is a proven identity.

ev-la-eigen.title: Essence of Linear Algebra — Eigenvectors and eigenvalues
ev-la-eigen.strength: Defines Av=λv as the directions a transformation only scales, with the rotation/complex-eigenvalue caveat; canonical explainer of settled theory.

ev-prob-basics.title: Seeing Theory — Basic Probability
ev-prob-basics.strength: Interactive visual probability textbook from Brown; introduces sample spaces and P=favourable/total. Expository teaching reference for settled definitions.

ev-prob-rules.title: Seeing Theory — Compound Probability
ev-prob-rules.strength: Brown's interactive stats text; covers the addition/multiplication rules and independence with animations. Definitional, not contested.

ev-prob-conditional.title: Conditional probability
ev-prob-conditional.strength: Tertiary encyclopaedia article giving the standard definition P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B) and the prosecutor's-fallacy caveat. Settled maths; well-cited.

ev-prob-bayes.title: Seeing Theory — Bayesian Inference
ev-prob-bayes.strength: Brown's interactive text on priors, likelihoods and posteriors; visualises updating. The theorem is proven; the frequentist/Bayesian interpretive split noted in the card is a real, live debate.

ev-prob-random-variable.title: Seeing Theory — Probability Distributions
ev-prob-random-variable.strength: Brown's interactive text introducing random variables (discrete vs continuous) and their distributions. Expository, settled content.

ev-prob-expectation.title: Expected value
ev-prob-expectation.strength: Tertiary article giving E[X]=Σ xᵢpᵢ, the fair-die example and the utility caveat. Settled definition; heavily referenced.

ev-prob-variance.title: Variance
ev-prob-variance.strength: Tertiary article defining σ²=E[(X−μ)²] and its outlier-sensitivity. Settled maths; well-sourced to standard texts.

ev-prob-distributions.title: Seeing Theory — Probability Distributions
ev-prob-distributions.strength: Brown's interactive text covering the uniform, Bernoulli and binomial shapes with animated sampling. Definitional.

ev-prob-normal.title: Normal distribution
ev-prob-normal.strength: Tertiary article giving the Gaussian density, the 68–95 rule and the fat-tails caveat. Settled maths; extensively referenced.

ev-stat-descriptive.title: Median
ev-stat-descriptive.strength: Tertiary article that directly contrasts mean vs median on skewed (e.g. income) data — the card's central point. Settled descriptive statistics.

ev-stat-sampling.title: Seeing Theory — Frequentist Inference
ev-stat-sampling.strength: Brown's interactive text on estimating a population from a sample and how error shrinks with n. The 1936 Literary Digest bias example is a documented historical case.

ev-stat-hypothesis.title: ASA Statement on p-Values and Statistical Significance
ev-stat-hypothesis.strength: The professional body's formal consensus statement; directly defines the p-value and lists its common misuses — primary authority for the card's caveat.

ev-stat-confidence.title: Seeing Theory — Frequentist Inference
ev-stat-confidence.strength: Brown's interactive text visualising confidence intervals across repeated samples — exactly the long-run interpretation (vs the common misreading) the card flags.

ev-stat-regression.title: Seeing Theory — Regression Analysis
ev-stat-regression.strength: Brown's interactive text on least-squares regression, minimising squared residuals, with the line fitted live. Expository, settled method.

ev-ml-what.title: Machine Learning — What is Machine Learning?
ev-ml-what.strength: Google's maintained ML course; frames a model as a learned function with parameters and notes data-driven bias. Authoritative practitioner reference.

ev-ml-linear-regression.title: Machine Learning Crash Course — Linear Regression
ev-ml-linear-regression.strength: Google's ML course chapter presenting ŷ as a weighted sum of features with learned weights and bias. Standard treatment.

ev-ml-loss.title: Machine Learning Crash Course — Linear Regression: Loss
ev-ml-loss.strength: Google's ML course chapter defining MSE and why squaring penalises large errors. Standard, with the loss-choice caveat the card raises.

ev-ml-gradient-descent.title: Machine Learning Crash Course — Linear Regression: Gradient Descent
ev-ml-gradient-descent.strength: Google's ML course chapter on the w ← w − η∇L update and the learning-rate trade-off, including local-minimum risk. Authoritative.

ev-ml-logistic.title: Machine Learning Crash Course — Logistic Regression
ev-ml-logistic.strength: Google's ML course chapter on the sigmoid squashing a weighted sum into a 0–1 probability, plus calibration caveats. Standard treatment.

ev-ml-perceptron.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning — Ch. 1
ev-ml-perceptron.strength: Widely used free online book; Ch. 1 builds the perceptron and sigmoid neuron (weighted sum + activation) from scratch. Expository, with the loose brain-analogy caveat the card flags.

ev-ml-neural-net.title: Neural Networks — But what is a Neural Network?
ev-ml-neural-net.strength: Canonical visual lesson showing a layer as a matrix multiply plus bias plus activation. Expository explainer; the universal-approximation point is a known existence result.

ev-ml-backprop.title: Neural Networks — What is backpropagation really doing?
ev-ml-backprop.strength: Well-known visual lesson presenting backprop as the chain rule applied backward through layers. Expository; vanishing-gradient caveat is established.

ev-ml-softmax-crossentropy.title: Softmax function
ev-ml-softmax-crossentropy.strength: Tertiary article giving the softmax formula and its use as a normalised probability output (incl. the link to cross-entropy). Settled, well-referenced.

ev-ml-overfitting.title: Machine Learning Crash Course — Overfitting
ev-ml-overfitting.strength: Google's ML course chapter on overfitting, generalisation and held-out evaluation. Standard; the double-descent caveat the card adds is a recognised modern finding.

ev-ml-attention.who: Vaswani, Shazeer, Parmar, Uszkoreit, Jones, Gomez, Kaiser, Polosukhin
ev-ml-attention.title: Attention Is All You Need
ev-ml-attention.strength: The primary, foundational transformer paper (>100k citations); defines scaled dot-product attention softmax(QKᵀ/√d)V used by modern LLMs. The interpretability caveat cites Jain & Wallace (2019).

ev-fin-time-value.title: Time value of money
ev-fin-time-value.strength: Tertiary article giving FV = PV(1+r)ⁿ and the discounting logic. Settled finance fundamentals; well-referenced to standard texts.

ev-fin-compound-interest.title: Compound interest
ev-fin-compound-interest.strength: Tertiary article covering compounding, the exponential formula and the Rule of 72. Settled maths of money; the borrower/saver symmetry the card notes is uncontested.

ev-fin-present-value.title: Present value
ev-fin-present-value.strength: Tertiary article giving PV = FV/(1+r)ⁿ and the discount-rate sensitivity the card flags. Settled definition; well-cited.

ev-fin-npv-irr.title: Net present value
ev-fin-npv-irr.strength: Tertiary article with the NPV sum and the NPV-vs-IRR caveats (multiple IRRs, scale) the card raises. Standard corporate-finance content.

ev-fin-risk-return.title: Risk–return spectrum
ev-fin-risk-return.strength: Tertiary article on the risk premium and the μ–σ trade-off. The behavioural caveat (loss aversion) is a separate, well-documented finding.

ev-qf-diversification.who: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences / NobelPrize.org
ev-qf-diversification.title: Harry M. Markowitz — Facts (1990 Prize in Economic Sciences)
ev-qf-diversification.strength: Official Nobel page recognising Markowitz's 1952 portfolio theory — the primary attribution for diversification as risk reduction. The 'correlations spike in a crash' caveat is a documented empirical pattern.

ev-qf-capm.who: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences / NobelPrize.org
ev-qf-capm.title: William F. Sharpe — Facts (1990 Prize in Economic Sciences)
ev-qf-capm.strength: Official Nobel page for Sharpe's CAPM. The card's caveat that beta predicts returns poorly cites Fama & French (1992), the standard empirical challenge.

ev-qf-efficient-market.who: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences / NobelPrize.org
ev-qf-efficient-market.title: Eugene F. Fama — Facts (2013 Prize in Economic Sciences)
ev-qf-efficient-market.strength: Official Nobel page for Fama's efficient-markets work; the 2013 prize was shared with Robert Shiller, whose opposing behavioural view the card names — the dispute is genuinely live.

ev-qf-random-walk.title: Random walk hypothesis
ev-qf-random-walk.strength: Tertiary article on the random-walk model of prices and Malkiel's argument, plus the documented momentum/fat-tail challenges the card's counter raises.

ev-qf-options.title: Option (finance)
ev-qf-options.strength: Tertiary article defining calls/puts, strike, and the max(0,S−K) payoff. Settled definitions; the seller's uncapped-risk caveat is uncontested.

ev-qf-black-scholes.who: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences / NobelPrize.org
ev-qf-black-scholes.title: The Prize in Economic Sciences 1997 — Press release (Scholes & Merton)
ev-qf-black-scholes.strength: Official Nobel announcement of the Black–Scholes–Merton method (Black having died in 1995). Authoritative attribution; the assumptions-fail-in-crises caveat (1987, LTCM 1998) is well-documented history.

ev-qf-bond-yield.title: Bond valuation
ev-qf-bond-yield.strength: Tertiary article giving the present-value bond price and the inverse price–yield relationship plus duration. Settled fixed-income maths.

ev-qf-leverage-risk.title: Leverage (finance)
ev-qf-leverage-risk.strength: Tertiary article on how borrowing magnifies returns and losses. The VaR/tail-risk critique the card attributes to Taleb, and the LTCM/2008 cases, are documented.

ev-re-mortgage.title: Mortgage loan
ev-re-mortgage.strength: Tertiary article covering amortization and the level-payment formula; the interest-then-principal split is settled arithmetic. The ARM caveat the card raises is documented.

ev-re-ltv-equity.title: Loan-to-value ratio
ev-re-ltv-equity.strength: Tertiary article defining LTV and its role in lending risk; the leverage-magnifies-equity point is straightforward arithmetic.

ev-re-noi-caprate.title: Capitalization rate
ev-re-noi-caprate.strength: Tertiary article giving cap rate = NOI/price and its use as a yield; settled definition, with the caveat that it ignores financing and growth.

ev-re-valuation.title: Real estate appraisal
ev-re-valuation.strength: Tertiary article laying out the three standard approaches (sales-comparison, income, cost). Established appraisal practice; the 'breaks in thin markets' caveat is well documented.

ev-re-reit.title: Real estate investment trust
ev-re-reit.strength: Tertiary article on REIT structure and the income-distribution rule (≈90% in the US). The 'trades like equities' caveat reflects documented return correlations.

ev-re-rate-sensitivity.title: Real estate economics
ev-re-rate-sensitivity.strength: Tertiary article on the determinants of property prices, including interest rates and affordability. The link is mainstream; the lag/supply caveat the card adds is real.

ev-re-bubble.title: Real-estate bubble
ev-re-bubble.strength: Tertiary article on housing bubbles and the 2000s episode. The Shiller-vs-Fama dispute over whether bubbles are identifiable in advance is genuine and named in the card.

ev-pf-taxation.title: Tax
ev-pf-taxation.strength: Tertiary article surveying tax types and progressive/flat/regressive structures. Settled categories; the fairness debate the card flags is genuinely political, not settled.

ev-pf-tax-incidence.title: Tax incidence
ev-pf-tax-incidence.strength: Tertiary article on legal vs economic incidence and the role of elasticity. Standard public economics; the corporate-tax incidence estimate range the card notes is an active research question.

ev-pf-deadweight-laffer.title: Laffer curve
ev-pf-deadweight-laffer.strength: Tertiary article on the revenue curve and its zero-at-both-ends shape. The shape is uncontested; where the peak sits (and the CBO/most-economists view that it's far above current rates) is the documented dispute the card names.

ev-pf-public-goods.title: Public good (economics)
ev-pf-public-goods.strength: Tertiary article on Samuelson's non-rival/non-excludable definition and the free-rider problem. The Ostrom/Coase counter-examples the card cites are well established.

ev-pf-deficit-debt.title: Government debt
ev-pf-deficit-debt.strength: Tertiary article distinguishing deficit (flow) from debt (stock) and using debt-to-GDP. Settled accounting; the 'how much is too much' question is explicitly contested.

ev-pf-fiscal-policy.title: Fiscal policy
ev-pf-fiscal-policy.strength: Tertiary article on demand management, the multiplier and crowding-out. The Keynes-vs-austerity dispute, and the Reinhart-Rogoff spreadsheet error (Herndon et al. 2013), are documented and named.

ev-pf-debt-sustainability.title: Public Debt and Low Interest Rates (AEA Presidential Address)
ev-pf-debt-sustainability.strength: Primary, peer-reviewed source for the r-versus-g framing and the argument that debt is less alarming when r<g. The card names the opposing view (a sudden jump in r, as in 2022) as the live counter.

ev-qf-arbitrage.title: Arbitrage
ev-qf-arbitrage.strength: Tertiary article on arbitrage and the law of one price. Settled principle; the 'limits of arbitrage' caveat (Shleifer & Vishny) the card names is a documented finance result.

ev-qf-sharpe-ratio.title: Sharpe ratio
ev-qf-sharpe-ratio.strength: Tertiary article giving S=(R−Rf)/σ and its normality assumption. Settled definition; the downside-vs-upside critique (Sortino) is standard.

ev-qf-efficient-frontier.title: Efficient frontier
ev-qf-efficient-frontier.strength: Tertiary article on Markowitz's frontier and the capital market line. The 'error maximization' sensitivity caveat (Michaud) the card raises is well documented.

ev-qf-put-call-parity.title: Put–call parity
ev-qf-put-call-parity.strength: Tertiary article deriving C−P=S−Ke^(−rt) from no-arbitrage. A proven identity for European options; dividend/early-exercise caveats are standard.

ev-qf-yield-curve.title: Yield curve
ev-qf-yield-curve.strength: Tertiary article on the curve's shapes and inversion as a recession signal. The empirical inversion-recession record is documented; the timing/term-premium caveats are noted.

ev-qf-factor-models.title: Fama–French three-factor model
ev-qf-factor-models.strength: Tertiary article on the size and value factors extending CAPM. The 'factor zoo' critique (Cochrane; McLean & Pontiff) the card names is an active research debate.

ev-re-dscr.title: Debt service coverage ratio
ev-re-dscr.strength: Tertiary article giving DSCR=NOI/debt service and typical lender thresholds. Settled lending metric; the NOI-can-be-flattered caveat is standard underwriting wisdom.

ev-re-leverage-returns.title: Real estate investing
ev-re-leverage-returns.strength: Tertiary article covering leverage and returns in property, including positive/negative leverage. The cap-rate-vs-borrowing-cost framing is settled arithmetic.

ev-re-mbs.title: Mortgage-backed security
ev-re-mbs.strength: Tertiary article on securitization, tranches and the 2008 role of MBS/CDOs. The structure-vs-underwriting blame dispute (FCIC, Lewis) the card names is documented.

ev-re-property-cycle.title: Real estate cycle
ev-re-property-cycle.strength: Tertiary article on the property cycle; the price=NOI/cap-rate mechanics and cap-rate compression/expansion are settled. Timing difficulty and the public/private lag are well known.

ev-re-development.title: Real estate development
ev-re-development.strength: Tertiary article on development; the residual-land-value method and its sensitivity to assumptions are standard appraisal practice.

ev-pf-pigouvian.title: Pigouvian tax
ev-pf-pigouvian.strength: Tertiary article on taxing externalities at the social-harm rate. The Pigou-vs-Coase dispute the card names is a foundational and genuinely unsettled debate.

ev-pf-redistribution-gini.title: Gini coefficient
ev-pf-redistribution-gini.strength: Tertiary article on the Lorenz curve and the 0–1 Gini measure. Settled definition; the 'one number hides the shape' caveat is widely made by inequality researchers.

ev-pf-fiscal-multiplier.title: Fiscal multiplier
ev-pf-fiscal-multiplier.strength: Tertiary article on the multiplier and its state-dependence. The disputed size (Blanchard & Leigh 2013 vs Alesina) the card names is a real, ongoing macro debate.

ev-pf-monetary-vs-fiscal.title: Monetary policy
ev-pf-monetary-vs-fiscal.strength: Tertiary article on central-bank rate-setting and independence, contrasted with fiscal policy. The zero-lower-bound and QE blurring caveats are standard.

ev-pf-mmt.title: Modern Monetary Theory
ev-pf-mmt.strength: Tertiary article on MMT and its critics. The card frames it explicitly as a live dispute — Kelton et al. vs Summers/Rogoff/Krugman — which the article documents.

ev-micro-opportunity-cost.title: Opportunity cost
ev-micro-opportunity-cost.strength: Tertiary article on opportunity cost and sunk costs. Settled foundational concept; the opportunity-cost-neglect finding (Frederick et al.) the card cites is documented behavioural research.

ev-micro-margin.title: Marginalism
ev-micro-margin.strength: Tertiary article on marginal analysis and the marginal-benefit-equals-marginal-cost rule. Core, settled microeconomic method.

ev-micro-marginal-utility.title: Marginal utility
ev-micro-marginal-utility.strength: Tertiary article on diminishing marginal utility and its link to demand. Standard theory; the card's caveat that utility is ordinal, not measurable, reflects the modern consensus.

ev-micro-elasticity.title: Price elasticity of demand
ev-micro-elasticity.strength: Tertiary article giving E=%ΔQ/%ΔP and the elastic/inelastic distinction. Settled definition; the 'varies along the curve and over time' caveat is standard.

ev-micro-surplus.title: Economic surplus
ev-micro-surplus.strength: Tertiary article on consumer/producer surplus and deadweight loss. Standard welfare analysis; the 'dollars not need' fairness caveat is widely made.

ev-micro-economies-of-scale.title: Economies of scale
ev-micro-economies-of-scale.strength: Tertiary article on scale economies, the U-shaped cost curve and minimum efficient scale. Settled; the near-zero-marginal-cost natural-monopoly point is well documented.

ev-micro-perfect-competition.title: Perfect competition
ev-micro-perfect-competition.strength: Tertiary article on the price-taker benchmark and its assumptions. The card stresses, as the article does, that it is an idealised benchmark rather than a description of real markets.

ev-micro-monopoly.title: Monopoly
ev-micro-monopoly.strength: Tertiary article on monopoly pricing, deadweight loss and antitrust. The Bork/Chicago vs neo-Brandeisian (Khan) antitrust dispute the card names is a real, current debate.

ev-micro-oligopoly.title: Oligopoly
ev-micro-oligopoly.strength: Tertiary article on few-firm strategic interaction and collusion. The prisoner's-dilemma framing and the difficulty of proving tacit collusion are standard.

ev-micro-price-discrimination.title: Price discrimination
ev-micro-price-discrimination.strength: Tertiary article on charging by willingness to pay and the conditions (market power, no resale). The ambiguous-welfare and fairness caveats are standard.

ev-micro-market-failure.title: Market failure
ev-micro-market-failure.strength: Tertiary article cataloguing externalities, public goods, market power and information failures. The 'government failure' counter (Buchanan, Hayek) the card raises is a recognised school.

ev-micro-asymmetric-info.who: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences / NobelPrize.org
ev-micro-asymmetric-info.title: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2001 — Press release (Akerlof, Spence, Stiglitz)
ev-micro-asymmetric-info.strength: Official Nobel announcement for the analysis of markets with asymmetric information, including Akerlof's 'lemons' and Spence's signalling — primary attribution for the card's claims.

ev-micro-adverse-selection.title: Adverse selection
ev-micro-adverse-selection.strength: Tertiary article on adverse selection in insurance and the role of screening/mandates. Settled mechanism; the fairness-of-mandates caveat is a genuine policy dispute.

ev-micro-moral-hazard.title: Moral hazard
ev-micro-moral-hazard.strength: Tertiary article on hidden action and the 'too big to fail' debate. Standard; the card flags the contested claim that moral hazard is overused to justify denying help.

ev-micro-principal-agent.title: Principal–agent problem
ev-micro-principal-agent.strength: Tertiary article on delegation, misaligned incentives and contract design. The backfiring-incentives caveat (Enron, gaming metrics) the card cites is well documented.

ev-micro-labour-market.who: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences / NobelPrize.org
ev-micro-labour-market.title: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2021 — Press release (Card, Angrist, Imbens)
ev-micro-labour-market.strength: Official Nobel announcement recognising David Card's natural-experiment work, including the Card–Krueger finding that minimum-wage rises need not cut employment — the live debate the card centres on.

ev-macro-inflation.title: Inflation
ev-macro-inflation.strength: Tertiary article on inflation, CPI and central-bank targets. Settled measurement; the card's caveat that the headline hides variation and disputed causes is standard.

ev-macro-real-nominal.title: Fisher equation
ev-macro-real-nominal.strength: Tertiary article giving r ≈ i − π and the real/nominal distinction. Settled identity; the expected-inflation caveat is standard.

ev-macro-unemployment.title: Unemployment
ev-macro-unemployment.strength: Tertiary article on the unemployment rate and its frictional/structural/cyclical types. The under-counting and 'natural rate is estimated' caveats are well documented.

ev-macro-phillips-curve.title: Phillips curve
ev-macro-phillips-curve.strength: Tertiary article on the inflation-unemployment trade-off and its expectations-driven breakdown (Friedman, Phelps). The recent-flatness debate the card names is live.

ev-macro-money-creation.title: Money creation
ev-macro-money-creation.strength: Tertiary article on bank money creation, citing the Bank of England's 2014 account. The endogenous-money dispute (post-Keynesian vs monetarist) the card raises is real.

ev-macro-quantity-theory.title: Quantity theory of money
ev-macro-quantity-theory.strength: Tertiary article on MV=PY and monetarism. The card's caveat on unstable velocity (post-2008/QE) is a documented, central objection.

ev-macro-business-cycle.title: Business cycle
ev-macro-business-cycle.strength: Tertiary article on expansions and recessions. The competing causal schools the card names (Keynesian, monetarist, real-business-cycle) are accurately represented.

ev-macro-ad-as.title: AD–AS model
ev-macro-ad-as.strength: Tertiary article on the aggregate demand/supply model. Standard teaching framework; the card flags the genuine disputes over its curves' shape and stability.

ev-macro-multiplier.title: Multiplier (economics)
ev-macro-multiplier.strength: Tertiary article giving the 1/(1−c) multiplier and the role of the marginal propensity to consume. Leakage and crowding-out caveats are standard.

ev-macro-growth-solow.title: Solow–Swan model
ev-macro-growth-solow.strength: Tertiary article on the Solow growth model, diminishing returns to capital and the technology residual. The endogenous-growth critique (Romer, 2018 Nobel) the card names is accurate.

ev-macro-exchange-rates.title: Exchange rate
ev-macro-exchange-rates.strength: Tertiary article on fixed vs floating rates and purchasing-power parity. The PPP-fails-short-run / overshooting (Dornbusch) and peg-crisis caveats are documented.

ev-macro-balance-of-payments.title: Balance of payments
ev-macro-balance-of-payments.strength: Tertiary article on the current and capital accounts and their accounting identity. Settled; the 'are deficits dangerous?' dispute the card raises is genuine.

ev-macro-liquidity-trap.title: Liquidity trap
ev-macro-liquidity-trap.strength: Tertiary article on the zero-lower-bound trap (Keynes, Japan, post-2008). The monetarist denial (Friedman, helicopter money) the card names is accurately represented.

ev-macro-hyperinflation.title: Hyperinflation
ev-macro-hyperinflation.strength: Tertiary article with the 50%/month benchmark and the Weimar/Zimbabwe/Venezuela cases. The monetarist-vs-fiscal-theory dispute over root cause is real.

ev-macro-gdp-critique.title: Gross domestic product
ev-macro-gdp-critique.strength: Tertiary article whose criticism section covers GDP's blind spots, Kuznets's 1934 warning and alternatives (HDI, GPI). The 'GDP was never meant to measure welfare' defence is also noted.

ev-macro-growth-debate.title: Degrowth
ev-macro-growth-debate.strength: Tertiary article on degrowth (Hickel, Kallis) vs green-growth/decoupling. The card presents both sides explicitly as a contested empirical debate, as the article does.

ev-pe-institutions.who: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences / NobelPrize.org
ev-pe-institutions.title: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2024 — Press release (Acemoglu, Johnson, Robinson)
ev-pe-institutions.strength: Official Nobel announcement for the work on how institutions shape prosperity — primary attribution. The Sachs (geography) and China-puzzle counters the card names are well-known critiques.

ev-pe-dependency.title: Dependency theory
ev-pe-dependency.strength: Tertiary article on Prebisch, Frank and Wallerstein's core-periphery analysis. The East-Asian-tigers rebuttal the card raises is the standard mainstream objection.

ev-pe-developmental-state.title: Developmental state
ev-pe-developmental-state.strength: Tertiary article on state-led East Asian industrialisation; names Chang and the export-discipline model. The crony-capitalism/failed-cases counter is documented.

ev-pe-feminist-econ.title: Feminist economics
ev-pe-feminist-econ.strength: Tertiary article on unpaid care, Waring's critique of national accounts, and gendered assumptions in models. The 'pricing care is arbitrary' counter is a genuine dispute over economic value.

ev-eh-colonial-extraction.title: Drain of wealth theory
ev-eh-colonial-extraction.strength: Tertiary article on Naoroji's drain thesis and Patnaik's estimates for colonial India. The contested-scale counter (Tirthankar Roy) the card names reflects a real historiographical split.

ev-eh-asian-miracle.title: Four Asian Tigers
ev-eh-asian-miracle.strength: Tertiary article on the rapid East Asian catch-up. The markets-vs-state dispute (World Bank vs Amsden/Wade) and Krugman's 'perspiration' critique the card cites are well documented.

ev-eh-washington-consensus.title: Washington Consensus
ev-eh-washington-consensus.strength: Tertiary article on Williamson's term and structural adjustment, including the Stiglitz/Easterly critiques and Williamson's own complaint that it was misused. Mixed results are documented.

ev-eh-marshall-plan.title: Marshall Plan
ev-eh-marshall-plan.strength: Tertiary article on the 1948 European Recovery Program. The debate over its decisiveness (Milward's revisionism vs the conventional view) the card names is a real historiographical dispute.

ev-cyber-cia-triad.title: Information security
ev-cyber-cia-triad.strength: Tertiary article that defines the confidentiality–integrity–availability triad. Settled foundational framework; the card notes the standard critique that the triad is incomplete.

ev-cyber-threat-risk.title: Threat (computer security)
ev-cyber-threat-risk.strength: Tertiary article distinguishing threat, vulnerability, attack surface and risk. Standard terminology; the 'risk numbers are estimates' caveat is widely acknowledged.

ev-cyber-authentication.title: Multi-factor authentication
ev-cyber-authentication.strength: Tertiary article on authentication factors and MFA. The SIM-swap / push-fatigue weaknesses the card raises are documented attack techniques.

ev-cyber-passwords-hashing.title: Salt (cryptography)
ev-cyber-passwords-hashing.strength: Tertiary article on salting and password hashing against rainbow tables. Settled practice; NIST's 2017 reversal on rotation/complexity rules the card cites is well documented.

ev-cyber-symmetric-encryption.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
ev-cyber-symmetric-encryption.strength: Tertiary article on shared-key encryption (AES) and the key-distribution problem. The 'most failures are key-management failures' caveat is a standard practitioner point.

ev-cyber-public-key.title: Public-key cryptography
ev-cyber-public-key.strength: Tertiary article on asymmetric crypto and the public/private key pair, including RSA. The 'security rests on believed-hard problems, broken by Shor' caveat is accurate.

ev-cyber-tls.title: Transport Layer Security
ev-cyber-tls.strength: Tertiary article on the TLS handshake, certificates and the symmetric/asymmetric split. The CA-trust weakness the card flags is well documented.

ev-cyber-hashing-signatures.title: Digital signature
ev-cyber-hashing-signatures.strength: Tertiary article on hashing, signing and verification. The stolen-signing-key risk (Stuxnet, SolarWinds) the card cites is documented history.

ev-cyber-phishing.title: Phishing
ev-cyber-phishing.strength: Tertiary article on phishing, spear-phishing and business email compromise. The 'blaming users misses bad system design' counter is a recognised security-culture argument.

ev-cyber-malware.title: Malware
ev-cyber-malware.strength: Tertiary article taxonomising viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware and more. The ransomware-as-a-service industrialisation the card notes is documented.

ev-cyber-injection.title: SQL injection
ev-cyber-injection.strength: Tertiary article on injection via untrusted input and the parameterised-query fix. Injection's persistence atop the OWASP risk list the card cites is well established.

ev-cyber-mitm.title: Man-in-the-middle attack
ev-cyber-mitm.strength: Tertiary article on interception attacks and how TLS authentication defeats them. The SSL-stripping / rogue-CA caveats are documented.

ev-cyber-ddos.title: Denial-of-service attack
ev-cyber-ddos.strength: Tertiary article on DoS/DDoS and botnet floods. The Mirai/IoT escalation and extortion-smokescreen points the card raises are documented.

ev-cyber-buffer-overflow.title: Buffer overflow
ev-cyber-buffer-overflow.strength: Tertiary article on memory overflows, exploitation and mitigations (canaries, ASLR, NX). The NSA/CISA memory-safe-language push the card cites is recent official guidance.

ev-cyber-zero-day.title: Zero-day vulnerability
ev-cyber-zero-day.strength: Tertiary article on zero-days, the exploit market and disclosure. The EternalBlue/WannaCry stockpiling case the card cites is documented history.

ev-cyber-defense-in-depth.title: Defense in depth (computing)
ev-cyber-defense-in-depth.strength: Tertiary article on layered controls and least privilege. The 'security theatre' caveat the card raises is a recognised critique.

ev-cyber-threat-model.title: Threat model
ev-cyber-threat-model.strength: Tertiary article on threat modelling and frameworks like STRIDE. The 'only as good as its assumptions / rots over time' caveat is standard.

ev-cyber-zero-trust.title: NIST SP 800-207: Zero Trust Architecture
ev-cyber-zero-trust.strength: The primary US standards document defining zero-trust architecture — authoritative, not tertiary. The card's caveat that 'zero trust' is over-marketed is a common practitioner complaint.

ev-cyber-supply-chain.title: Supply chain attack
ev-cyber-supply-chain.strength: Tertiary article on upstream-compromise attacks, citing SolarWinds and dependency risks. The unpaid-maintainer 'Log4Shell' point the card raises is documented.

ev-cyber-post-quantum.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography project
ev-cyber-post-quantum.strength: The official NIST programme standardising post-quantum algorithms (first standards finalised 2024) — primary, authoritative. Shor's algorithm and the 'harvest now, decrypt later' threat the card describes are the project's stated rationale; the uncertain-timeline caveat is genuine.

ev-stat-ols.title: Ordinary least squares
ev-stat-ols.strength: Tertiary article giving the normal equations, the closed-form β̂ = (XᵀX)⁻¹Xᵀy, and the Gauss–Markov theorem. Settled estimator; the assumptions/outlier/multicollinearity caveats the card raises are standard.

ev-cyber-firewall.title: Firewall (computing)
ev-cyber-firewall.strength: Tertiary article on packet-filtering, stateful and next-gen firewalls. Settled technology; the 'useless against an attacker already inside' caveat motivates the zero-trust shift the card notes.

ev-cyber-vpn.title: Virtual private network
ev-cyber-vpn.strength: Tertiary article on VPN tunnelling and uses. The card's caveat that consumer-VPN marketing overpromises (HTTPS already encrypts; the provider can log) is a widely-made security-researcher critique.

ev-cyber-ids-ips.title: Intrusion detection system
ev-cyber-ids-ips.strength: Tertiary article on IDS/IPS and signature vs anomaly detection. The alert-fatigue failure (e.g. the 2013 Target breach) the card cites is documented.

ev-cyber-dns.title: DNS spoofing
ev-cyber-dns.strength: Tertiary article on cache poisoning and DNSSEC. The slow DNSSEC adoption and resolver-centralisation caveats the card raises are documented.

ev-cyber-access-control.title: Access control
ev-cyber-access-control.strength: Tertiary article covering DAC/MAC/RBAC and least privilege. The 'privilege creep' decay the card flags is a well-known audit finding.

ev-cyber-privilege-escalation.title: Privilege escalation
ev-cyber-privilege-escalation.strength: Tertiary article on vertical/horizontal escalation. The 'assume breach, limit blast radius' lesson the card draws is mainstream modern guidance.

ev-cyber-sandboxing.title: Sandbox (computer security)
ev-cyber-sandboxing.strength: Tertiary article on confinement and isolation. The valuable 'sandbox escape' bugs and sandbox-evading malware the card mentions are documented.

ev-cyber-incident-response.title: NIST SP 800-61: Computer Security Incident Handling Guide
ev-cyber-incident-response.strength: The primary US standards guide defining the prepare-detect-contain-eradicate-recover lifecycle — authoritative, not tertiary. The Equifax slow-response cautionary case the card cites is documented.

ev-cyber-logging-siem.title: Security information and event management
ev-cyber-logging-siem.strength: Tertiary article on log aggregation, correlation and alerting. The alert-overload and log-tampering caveats the card raises are standard SOC concerns.

ev-cyber-forensics.title: Digital forensics
ev-cyber-forensics.strength: Tertiary article on evidence collection, analysis and chain of custody. The anti-forensics and fragile-evidence caveats the card raises are documented.

ev-cyber-cloud-responsibility.title: Cloud computing security
ev-cyber-cloud-responsibility.strength: Tertiary article covering the shared-responsibility model and misconfiguration risk. That most cloud breaches are customer misconfiguration (public buckets, exposed keys) is well documented.

ev-cyber-containers.title: NIST SP 800-190: Application Container Security Guide
ev-cyber-containers.strength: The primary US standards guide on container security — authoritative. Covers shared-kernel isolation risks, image vulnerabilities and the don't-run-as-root guidance the card states.

ev-cyber-secrets.title: Secrets management
ev-cyber-secrets.strength: Tertiary article on storing keys/passwords/certificates and vault tooling. The 'don't hard-code secrets / bots scan repos' point and the 'vault becomes a target / secret sprawl' caveat are documented practice.

ev-german-reunification.title: German reunification
ev-german-reunification.strength: Tertiary article covering the Article 23 accession vs Article 146 (new-constitution) debate, the Treuhand privatisation and lasting East–West disparities — i.e. both the 'reunification' and the 'annexation/accession' readings the card presents. Well referenced; the interpretive dispute (Kohl/liberal vs PDS/Die Linke and East German critics) is genuinely live.

ev-micro-info-economics.title: Greenwald–Stiglitz theorem
ev-micro-info-economics.strength: Tertiary article on the theorem that economies with imperfect information or incomplete markets are not (constrained) Pareto efficient — Stiglitz's core challenge to the first welfare theorem. The Chicago/Hayek 'government failure' counter the card raises is a recognised, opposing position.

ev-macro-efficiency-wages.title: Shapiro–Stiglitz theory
ev-macro-efficiency-wages.strength: Tertiary article on the Shapiro–Stiglitz (1984) shirking model in which efficiency wages produce equilibrium involuntary unemployment. The new-classical objection that unemployment is largely voluntary/frictional, which the card names, is the standard counter-position.

ev-pe-stiglitz-inequality.title: The Price of Inequality
ev-pe-stiglitz-inequality.strength: Tertiary article on Stiglitz's 2012 book arguing inequality is policy-driven (rent-seeking) and growth-harming. The Mankiw 'Defending the One Percent' marginal-productivity rebuttal the card names is a real, opposing academic position.

ev-ir-what-is.title: International relations
ev-ir-what-is.strength: Broad expository overview of the discipline. Verified against the Wikipedia articles on Man, the State, and War (book year 1959; three images; Waltz favours the third) and Alexander Wendt (1992 'Anarchy Is What States Make of It'). The discipline's boundaries and dominant theories are contested, which the article flags.

ev-ir-anarchy.title: Anarchy (international relations)
ev-ir-anarchy.strength: Fetch-verified canonical entry that explicitly distinguishes anarchy from chaos ('not a world in chaos, disorder, or conflict') and lays out the realist, liberal and constructivist readings; it names Wendt as the leading constructivist and cites his 1992 International Organization article by title. The interpretive disagreement it documents is genuine and live.

ev-ir-realism.who: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (W. Julian Korab-Karpowicz)
ev-ir-realism.title: Political Realism in International Relations
ev-ir-realism.strength: Peer-reviewed encyclopedia entry that directly covers Thucydides' Melian Dialogue, Hobbes, Carr and Morgenthau's 'interest defined as power', the prudence-vs-moralism distinction, and the named neoliberal (Keohane) and constructivist (Wendt, 'anarchy is what states make of it') critiques; a tertiary survey that maps the tradition and its variants rather than adjudicating between them.

ev-ir-neorealism.title: Neorealism (international relations)
ev-ir-neorealism.strength: Expository entry that sources structural realism to Waltz's 1979 Theory of International Politics, identifies defensive realism with Waltz and Jervis's 1978 security-dilemma article and offensive realism with Mearsheimer's 2001 book aiming at regional hegemony, and lists Wendt among constructivist critics; the offensive-vs-defensive debate it reports is unresolved among realists themselves.

ev-ir-balance-of-power.title: Balance of power (international relations)
ev-ir-balance-of-power.strength: Canonical encyclopedia entry covering balancing vs bandwagoning, Waltz's automatic-balancing claim, and a dedicated section on Walt's balance of threat (1985 article, 1987 book); it cites a 2021 assessment that balance of power 'is not a universal empirical law,' supporting the contested status in the counter. Walt's four threat factors and Morgenthau's treatment are corroborated by the Balance of threat entry and Politics Among Nations scholarship.

ev-ir-liberalism.title: Liberalism (international relations)
ev-ir-liberalism.strength: Tertiary survey of the tradition (Kant, commercial and republican liberalism, and Keohane and Nye's complex interdependence). Thin on the realist relative-gains rebuttal and on dependency-school criticism, and its core causal claim — does trade really pacify? — remains empirically contested.

ev-ir-democratic-peace.title: Democratic peace theory
ev-ir-democratic-peace.strength: Expository entry covering Kant's Perpetual Peace, Doyle's two-part 1983 essay, Russett on normative and institutional mechanisms, the monadic/dyadic distinction, and a substantial section on Sebastian Rosato's 2003 APSR critique. It reports a genuinely contested literature: the dyadic empirical pattern is strong, but its causes (regime type vs. shared interests, alliances and US power) are disputed.

ev-ir-institutions.title: Liberal institutionalism
ev-ir-institutions.strength: Fetch-verified: the page states Keohane's mechanisms (transaction costs, information, credible commitments, the shadow of the future) from 'After Hegemony' (1984) and Mearsheimer's realist rebuttal in 'The False Promise of International Institutions' (International Security, 1994), so it presents the institutionalist-vs-realist debate as live rather than settled. It does not substantively cover the constructivist critique (Wendt) added in the detail, which is a separate well-documented position.

ev-ir-constructivism.title: Constructivism (international relations)
ev-ir-constructivism.strength: Tertiary survey of a major theoretical school; fetch-verified to attribute the core claims to Wendt's 1992 International Organization article and the norm life-cycle and 'norm entrepreneurs' to Finnemore and Sikkink, to record Mearsheimer's realist objection that ideas matter only on the margins, and to list non-Western (Qin Yaqing) and feminist constructivist strands. The British/North Korean nuclear example is Wendt's own and is documented in coverage of the 1992 article.

ev-ir-marxist-critical.title: World-systems theory
ev-ir-marxist-critical.strength: Fetch-verified: a live encyclopaedic account of Wallerstein's core/periphery/semi-periphery framework and its debt to and break from dependency theory. A contested, normatively loaded research programme, which the entry presents as one school among several rather than as established fact.

ev-ir-english-school.title: English school of international relations theory
ev-ir-english-school.strength: Expository entry centred on Bull's 'The Anarchical Society' (1977) and Wight's three traditions; states Bull's five institutions (diplomacy, international law, balance of power, great powers, war) and the order/justice tension, and flags recent revisions addressing the school's Eurocentrism. Does not itself detail the Gong/Keene 'standard of civilisation' critique, which is sourced from those authors' own works named in the counter.

ev-ir-hegemonic-stability.title: Hegemonic stability theory
ev-ir-hegemonic-stability.strength: Tertiary overview that credits Kindleberger's 'The World in Depression' (1973) as the founding argument, names Gilpin and Krasner as generalisers, and records that Keohane coined the label in 1980 and rebutted it in 'After Hegemony' (1984); Snidal's sustainability critique is also covered, so the public-goods/necessity claim is presented as contested. Verified by fetch. Organski's 1958 'World Politics' authorship of power-transition theory and the Allison/Nye 'Thucydides Trap' dispute were cross-checked against the Power transition theory and Thucydides Trap Wikipedia entries.

ev-ir-soft-power.title: Soft power
ev-ir-soft-power.strength: Canonical entry; attributes the concept to Nye, quotes his 1990 'Bound to Lead' coinage and his three resources (culture, political values, foreign policies), and names critics — Niall Ferguson (dismisses it), neorealists (force/incentives only), and Janice Bially Mattern (some attraction is disguised coercion). Verified by fetch June 2026.

ev-ir-deterrence.title: Deterrence theory
ev-ir-deterrence.strength: Tertiary survey covering Schelling's game-theoretic framing, MAD, second-strike credibility and the stability-instability paradox; fetch-verified to confirm the second-strike and stability-instability content. Whether deterrence 'worked' or Cold War survival was luck remains genuinely contested (Waltz vs Sagan); the Schelling dates, the Snyder attribution of the stability-instability paradox, and Sagan's 'Limits of Safety' (1993) were cross-checked against their own Wikipedia and publisher pages.

ev-ir-collective-security.title: Collective security
ev-ir-collective-security.strength: Tertiary overview that defines the concept, contrasts it explicitly with alliances (universal one-for-all membership vs. two blocs), and traces the League (first large-scale attempt) and the UN (a balance between collective action and the states system). It is light on Chapter VII veto mechanics and on free-riding, and it cites Inis Claude mainly on balance of power; the realist (Carr) vs. liberal verdict on whether collective security can ever work is openly contested, so dates and named thinkers here were cross-checked against sources on Carr's Twenty Years' Crisis (1939) and Claude's Power and International Relations (1962).

ev-ir-international-law.title: International law
ev-ir-international-law.strength: Tertiary reference; fetch-verified to cover pacta sunt servanda ('states create legal obligations on themselves through consent'), customary law as state practice plus opinio juris, treaties (VCLT Art. 2), and the absence of a universal authority to enforce law on sovereign states. The competing realist/liberal/constructivist explanations for *why* states comply, and the TWAIL critique of the framing, are a live scholarly debate the article only sketches.

ev-ir-global-governance.title: Global governance
ev-ir-global-governance.strength: Tertiary overview defining governance without an overarching authority and naming the UN, WTO, and international regimes. It does not itself cover the democratic-deficit debate, so the critique and counter rest on the named scholars (Keohane and Nye; global-South commentators), and what counts as legitimate global authority is genuinely disputed.

ev-ir-feminist.title: Feminism in international relations
ev-ir-feminist.strength: Tertiary survey covering Enloe, Tickner, the gendering of war/security/the state, the masculine 'rational actor' critique, the liberal/difference/poststructural splits, and the Keohane critique that feminists should proceed 'scientifically'. The Tickner-Keohane exchange (ISQ 1997-1998) and the Enloe edition dates are corroborated by the dedicated 'Bananas, Beaches and Bases' page and journal records. As living critical theory its claims are openly contested by both mainstream IR and rival feminist camps.

ev-ir-postcolonial.title: Postcolonialism (international relations)
ev-ir-postcolonial.strength: Fetch-verified tertiary reference covering Said's Orientalism (1978), Spivak's subaltern, and Du Bois's colour line and Fanon in IR. It does not name Acharya's 'Global IR'; that is attributed in the card to his 2014 ISA presidential address 'Global International Relations (IR) and Regional Worlds', later published in International Studies Quarterly 58(4):647-659. The Shilliam critique reflects the 'radicalising Global IR' strand. A contested, actively developing critical field.

ev-poli-what-is.title: Political science
ev-poli-what-is.strength: Tertiary/expository; the page explicitly contrasts the discipline's descriptive/explanatory 'what is' with normative political philosophy ('emphasizes descriptive and explanatory means of articulating what is ... favors empirical evidence over ethical judgements') and lists its empirical methods (surveys, case studies, experiments, process tracing). It also notes the behavioral revolution and the 'is it a science?' debate (quoting Lawrence Lowell that politics is observational, not experimental). Lasswell's 1936 title and Strauss's critique of Weber are verified against Britannica/APSR and the SEP entry on Leo Strauss respectively.

ev-poli-power.title: Feminist Perspectives on Power
ev-poli-power.strength: Strong tertiary/peer-reviewed reference. Explicitly attributes the one-dimensional view to Dahl (quoting his 1957 'get B to do something B would not otherwise do'), the two-dimensional view to Bachrach & Baratz, and the three-dimensional view to Lukes (1974, 2005), and notes Lukes frames all three as one underlying conception of power. Power is described as an essentially contested concept; the reality and measurability of the third face remain genuinely disputed between Lukes and the pluralists, and feminists critique its residual 'power over' framing.

ev-poli-state.title: Monopoly on violence
ev-poli-state.strength: Tertiary but quotes Weber's definition directly ('claim to the monopoly of the legitimate use of physical force'), traced to the 1919 lecture 'Politics as a Vocation' and 'Economy and Society' (1921-22). Canonical in the field; the page itself notes the monopoly is contested empirically (e.g. Raymond Aron on inter-state force) and by anarchists.

ev-poli-sovereignty.title: Sovereignty
ev-poli-sovereignty.strength: Authoritative SEP entry by Daniel Philpott (substantive revision Sept 2024). Verified by fetch to cover Bodin's above-the-law sovereign, Hobbes's contractual transfer of rights to the Leviathan, the internal/external distinction, the Westphalian model and its circumscription by human rights, the EU and R2P, and to report (via Krasner) the live contestation over whether Westphalia deserves its foundational status.

ev-poli-legitimacy.title: Political Legitimacy
ev-poli-legitimacy.strength: Fetch-verified. SEP entry states Weber's three sources verbatim ('tradition… charisma… legality—specifically the rationality of the rule of law') and explicitly separates the descriptive concept ('people's beliefs about political authority') from the normative one, naming Rawls (1993) and Raz's service conception as normative accounts.
