Pateman's feminist critique is from a separate, well-documented source (The Sexual Contract, 1988).

ev-poli-regime-types.title: Competitive authoritarianism
ev-poli-regime-types.strength: Tertiary but accurate for this card. The page sets out Levitsky & Way's concept (2002 Journal of Democracy article; 2010 book Competitive Authoritarianism) as a subtype of authoritarianism / hybrid regime: real multiparty elections combined with an unfair playing field, situated against democracy, authoritarianism and totalitarianism. Friedrich & Brzezinski's 1956 six-point totalitarian 'syndrome', Arendt's 1951 Origins of Totalitarianism, and Sartori's 1970 'concept stretching' are well-documented standard attributions verified separately. Whether to use discrete types or a continuous scale is genuinely debated in the field.

ev-poli-democracy.title: Democracy
ev-poli-democracy.strength: Authoritative SEP entry (first published 2006, substantively revised 18 June 2024) covering procedural vs substantive and instrumental vs intrinsic justifications; explicitly discusses Schumpeter's elite/competitive view and Dahl, and foregrounds that the definition itself is contested rather than settling it.

ev-poli-authoritarianism.title: Selectorate theory
ev-poli-authoritarianism.strength: Encyclopaedic summary of the model from Bueno de Mesquita, Smith, Siverson and Morrow's The Logic of Political Survival (2003), including the selectorate/winning-coalition distinction and named criticism by Jessica Weeks on its measurability and behavioural assumptions; an influential but contested formalisation.

ev-poli-democratization.title: Waves of democracy
ev-poli-democratization.strength: Tertiary overview of Huntington's wave thesis (first wave 1828-1926, third from 1974) and reverse waves; the periodisation and the modernization-theory link are named interpretive frameworks (Huntington 1991; Lipset 1959; Przeworski-Limongi 1997), not settled fact.

ev-poli-backsliding.title: Democratic backsliding
ev-poli-backsliding.strength: Canonical overview that names Bermeo's 'executive aggrandizement' and Levitsky & Ziblatt's norms, and cites V-Dem data showing more countries autocratizing than democratizing since c. 2010 (Hungary, Turkey, India, Poland, Brazil, US among cases). The concept and its case list are actively contested, and the article itself flags disagreement over which countries qualify.

ev-poli-separation-powers.title: Separation of powers
ev-poli-separation-powers.strength: Tertiary source; fetch-verified to cover the doctrine from Polybius and Locke through Montesquieu's 1748 'Spirit of the Laws' (including the cited quote) to modern checks-and-balances. The core principle is settled; how strictly to separate versus fuse powers stays a live design debate the article covers.

ev-poli-presidential-parliamentary.title: Presidential system
ev-poli-presidential-parliamentary.strength: Expository overview contrasting presidential and parliamentary forms and presenting Linz's 'perils' critique (rigidity, zero-sum elections) with the named scholarly debate around it; the breakdown claim is a prominent but actively disputed hypothesis (see Cheibub 2007, Mainwaring), not settled consensus.

ev-poli-federalism.title: Federalism
ev-poli-federalism.strength: Peer-reviewed SEP entry (first published 2003, substantive revision Nov 2022); covers the division of sovereignty and subsidiarity directly. Expository on a settled concept while flagging real disputes; Riker's 1964 bargaining thesis and Stepan's 1999 'demos-constraining' argument are verified against their original sources, not just the SEP.

ev-poli-veto-players.title: Veto player
ev-poli-veto-players.strength: Tertiary summary of Tsebelis's 2002 book Veto Players: How Political Institutions Work (Princeton UP); accurately states the core stability result and the spatial-model basis, but does not mention Immergut's earlier 'veto points' lineage, which was verified separately against her 1990 Journal of Public Policy article.

ev-poli-bureaucracy.title: Bureaucracy
ev-poli-bureaucracy.strength: Fetch-verified tertiary source: accurately lays out Weber's ideal-type features, rational-legal authority and the 'iron cage', and names Merton's dysfunctions. It does not cover Lipsky's street-level discretion, Niskanen's budget-maximizing model, Dunleavy's bureau-shaping rebuttal or Ferguson's feminist critique — those attributions were verified against the books' own descriptions and the dedicated Wikipedia pages (Budget-maximizing model, Bureau-shaping model).

ev-poli-rule-of-law.title: The Rule of Law
ev-poli-rule-of-law.strength: Peer-reviewed SEP entry by Jeremy Waldron (first published 2016); authoritative on the formal/procedural vs substantive split, the rule-of-law vs rule-by-law contrast, Fuller's and Raz's formal accounts, and explicit that the thick conception is contested. Thompson's 'unqualified human good' phrase verified to the conclusion of Whigs and Hunters (1975).

ev-poli-ideologies.title: Left–right political spectrum
ev-poli-ideologies.strength: Tertiary overview; fetch-verified to confirm the 1789 National Assembly origin (revolution to the president's left, Ancien Régime to his right) and the 'Criticism' section stating a single axis is too simplistic. Nolan's identity as a libertarian activist and Libertarian Party co-founder verified against the English Wikipedia 'Nolan chart' article.

ev-poli-nationalism.title: Nationalism
ev-poli-nationalism.strength: Peer-reviewed SEP entry that cites Gellner 1983 and Anderson 1983/1991 on the modernity of nations and A. Smith 1986 on ethnic origins, and notes a dissenting deep-roots view (Gat 2013), so it presents the modern-vs-ancient question as contested. It does not cover Chatterjee; that postcolonial critique is verified separately against his The Nation and Its Fragments (1993).

ev-poli-populism.title: Populism
ev-poli-populism.strength: Tertiary survey that states Mudde's 'thin-centred ideology / pure people vs corrupt elite / general will' definition, gives the same left/right examples (Le Pen, Trump; Chavez, Sanders), and lays out the ideational-vs-Laclau/Mouffe (discursive 'logic') dispute even-handedly. Verified live; no dedicated Stanford Encyclopedia entry for 'populism' exists, so Wikipedia is the correct canonical page.

ev-poli-social-movements.title: Social movement
ev-poli-social-movements.strength: Tertiary overview with dedicated sections on resource mobilization (attributed to McCarthy and Zald), political-process/opportunity theory, and Tilly's repertoire of contention (the petition/strike/demonstration/boycott menu, verified against the linked Repertoire of contention and Political opportunity articles). The Melucci/Polletta cultural critique is corroborated by their own work, not the Wikipedia page alone. A maturing-but-contested literature; the cultural critique is acknowledged as a live alternative, not a footnote.

ev-poli-revolution.title: States and Social Revolutions
ev-poli-revolution.strength: Expository page on Skocpol's 1979 book; confirms the state-breakdown-plus-peasant-revolt mechanism and the France/Russia/China cases, and records named critiques of her demotion of agency and ideology, so the contestation is on the record. Davies' 1962 J-curve, Gurr's 1970 'Why Men Rebel', the Phillips quotation, Sewell's ideology critique and Kuran's cascade account were cross-checked against their own canonical pages.

ev-poli-clientelism.title: Clientelism
ev-poli-clientelism.strength: Tertiary entry that defines clientelism through the dyadic, contingent, hierarchical and iterated exchange of goods for support via patron-broker-client ties, sets the explicit contrast with formalised programmatic distribution, and notes the secret-ballot monitoring problem central to Stokes's work; a well-theorised comparative-politics concept.

ev-poli-political-culture.title: The Civic Culture
ev-poli-political-culture.strength: Expository page on Almond & Verba's 1963 book and its parochial/subject/participant typology, the foundation the Putnam social-capital literature builds on; a foundational but heavily critiqued framework, and the Tarrow, Pateman and feminist critiques are named and sourced separately.

ev-poli-civil-society.title: Civil society
ev-poli-civil-society.strength: Tertiary entry placing civil society as the 'third sector' between state and family and covering Tocqueville's associations, Habermas's public sphere, and Gramsci's hegemony reading. The Stanford Encyclopedia has no standalone 'civil society' entry (it appears within the Hegel and Habermas entries), so Wikipedia is the right canonical page for this exact topic; the concept is long-contested, with Gramscian, 'dark side' (Berman) and postcolonial (Chatterjee) readings present in the literature.

ev-epi-what-knowledge.who: SEP (Jonathan Jenkins Ichikawa and Matthias Steup)
ev-epi-what-knowledge.title: The Analysis of Knowledge
ev-epi-what-knowledge.strength: Authoritative SEP entry (substantive revision Jan 2026) that lays out the tripartite JTB analysis, attributes the refuting counterexamples to Gettier (1963), covers Williamson's knowledge-first dissent, and states plainly that no analysis of knowledge has been widely accepted — confirming this is a contested research area, not a settled definition. The named Nyaya/Gangesa comparison is corroborated by SEP's 'Epistemology in Classical Indian Philosophy' (rev. 2024).

ev-epi-gettier.who: SEP (Jonathan Jenkins Ichikawa and Matthias Steup)
ev-epi-gettier.title: The Analysis of Knowledge
ev-epi-gettier.strength: Peer-reviewed SEP entry that quotes Gettier's 1963 Case I (Smith, Jones and the ten coins) and surveys the proposed fixes (no-false-lemmas, safety, sensitivity, virtue accounts). Honest about contestation: it states plainly that 'no analysis has been widely accepted', and notes some epistemologists now reject analysing knowledge at all.

ev-epi-reliabilism.title: Reliabilist Epistemology
ev-epi-reliabilism.strength: Stanford Encyclopedia entry (first published 2008, substantive revision 2021) co-authored by Goldman, the view's originator — so it is expository but partisan toward reliabilism; it does lay out the generality problem (attributing it to Feldman 1985 and Conee & Feldman 1998) and BonJour's clairvoyant objection, and frames reliabilism as the 'paradigm of externalism' against evidentialism as the 'paradigm of internalism'.

ev-epi-skepticism.who: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (Juan Comesaña; orig. Peter Klein)
ev-epi-skepticism.title: Skepticism
ev-epi-skepticism.strength: Peer-reviewed SEP entry (first published 2001, substantive revision Jan 2026) covering Cartesian, Pyrrhonian and closure-based skepticism. Even-handed: it lays out the skeptical argument's force and the leading anti-skeptical replies (closure-denial, contextualism, Moorean reversal) rather than declaring a winner. For Putnam's brain-in-a-vat self-refutation, the dedicated SEP entry is at /entries/brain-vat/.

ev-epi-rationalism-empiricism.title: Rationalism vs. Empiricism
ev-epi-rationalism-empiricism.strength: Fetch-verified canonical SEP entry (first published 2004, substantive revision 2 Sep 2021). It frames the debate via the intuition/deduction, innate-knowledge and innate-concept theses, and explicitly cautions that the rationalist/empiricist labelling oversimplifies — noting that almost no thinker falls cleanly into one camp and that figures such as Hobbes, Berkeley, Conway, du Chatelet and Shepherd resist the grouping. So it treats the dichotomy as a useful frame, not a settled taxonomy.

ev-epi-a-priori.title: The Analytic/Synthetic Distinction (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
ev-epi-a-priori.strength: Peer-reviewed SEP survey (substantive revision June 2026) covering Kant's synthetic a priori (§1.1) and Quine's 'Two Dogmas' and confirmation holism (§3.4) in depth; the entry is explicit that whether a viable analytic/synthetic distinction survives Quine's attack remains genuinely contested, so it maps an open debate rather than delivering a verdict.

ev-epi-problem-induction.title: The Problem of Induction (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
ev-epi-problem-induction.strength: Authoritative SEP survey (first published 2018, substantive revision 2022) reconstructing Hume's two-horned dilemma — demonstrative reasoning can't prove the Uniformity Principle, probable reasoning is circular — and surveying the major responses (Bayesian, Strawsonian dissolution, Reichenbach's pragmatic vindication, the material theory). Hume's negative argument is widely regarded as sound; what remains contested is which 'solution' or dissolution to accept, which the entry presents even-handedly.

ev-epi-truth.title: Truth (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
ev-epi-truth.strength: Fetch-verified canonical SEP entry by Michael Glanzberg (substantive revision Jun 27, 2025). Maps correspondence (§1.1, naming Aristotle, Moore, Russell c.1910), coherence (§1.2, exemplified by Joachim 1906 and Blanshard 1939), pragmatist (§1.3, Peirce and James) and deflationary/redundancy theories incl. Ramsey and Horwich's minimalism (§5). A genuinely live dispute with no consensus winner; the entry surveys competing camps and their objections rather than endorsing one.

ev-epi-bayesian.who: Hanti Lin (SEP; rewriting William Talbott's original entry)
ev-epi-bayesian.title: Bayesian Epistemology (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
ev-epi-bayesian.strength: Current SEP entry, first published 2001 by Talbott, completely rewritten by Lin in 2022 and revised 2024. Fetch-verified to cover credences, probabilism, conditionalization, Bayes' theorem, Dutch-book arguments (attributing them to Ramsey 1926 and de Finetti 1937), the probability axioms, the problem of the priors (naming subjective Bayesians de Finetti/Savage vs objective Bayesians Jeffreys/Jaynes), and the problem of old evidence (Glymour 1980, Mercury case). Candid that Bayesianism's foundational arguments are themselves contested.

ev-epi-testimony.title: Epistemological Problems of Testimony (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
ev-epi-testimony.strength: Peer-reviewed SEP entry (completely rewritten version first published Apr 1, 2021, by Nick Leonard; last substantively revised Feb 16, 2023; the original entry was by Jonathan Adler). Traces reductionism to Hume and non-reductionism to Reid, and surveys Coady's circularity objection, Fricker's local reductionism, and Moran's assurance view. Expository on a question that remains actively disputed; presents the camps even-handedly.

ev-epi-fallibilism.title: Fallibilism (Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
ev-epi-fallibilism.strength: Dedicated, authored encyclopedia entry by epistemologist Stephen Hetherington. Confirms Peirce coined the term, names Descartes' Evil Genius as the foundationalist target, states the 'Fallible Knowledge Thesis' (knowledge from less-than-infallible justification), and discusses the 'self-doubting knowledge claim' that underlies the concessive-knowledge puzzle. Chosen over Wikipedia because it is authored and covers the philosophical detail; chosen because the Stanford Encyclopedia has no dedicated 'fallibilism' slug (the topic is handled inside its contextualism entry). The specific Rysiew/Lewis attributions in the counter are verified against Rysiew's 'Fallibilism, Epistemic Possibility, and Concessive Knowledge Attributions', not this page.

ev-epi-occam.title: Simplicity
ev-epi-occam.strength: Peer-reviewed encyclopedia entry (first published 2004, substantively revised 16 May 2022). Verified to treat Occam's razor as a tie-breaker among theories that 'explain the same set of facts equally well'; to distinguish epistemic vs methodological readings; to flag the entities-vs-equations trade-off ('reducing the ontology... only possible at the price of making it syntactically more complex'); and to source the named positions used here — Popper (simpler = more falsifiable), Swinburne 1997 ('ultimate a priori epistemic principle that simplicity is evidence for truth'), and Sober (parsimony 'always depend[s] on local background assumptions for [its] rational justification'). Ockham's own wording, the John Punch 1639 origin of the Latin slogan, and the precursors (Aristotle, Ptolemy, Duns Scotus) cross-checked against the English Wikipedia 'Occam's razor' article.

ev-epi-scientific-realism.title: Scientific Realism
ev-epi-scientific-realism.strength: Authoritative peer-reviewed expository entry on a genuinely contested debate. Fetch-verified to attribute the no-miracles argument to Putnam (1975, realism 'the only philosophy that doesn't make the success of science a miracle'), the pessimistic meta-induction to Laudan (1981, successful theories 'later rejected'), and to define van Fraassen's constructive empiricism via 'empirical adequacy' (1980). It lays out the live camps even-handedly rather than settling the question.

ev-epi-kuhn.title: Thomas Kuhn
ev-epi-kuhn.strength: Peer-reviewed scholarly entry by a leading Kuhn specialist (first published 2004, substantive revision 2 Sep 2025); fetch-verified to cover normal science as puzzle-solving, paradigms, crisis, revolutions, the three kinds of incommensurability (methodological, perceptual, semantic), and Kuhn's view set explicitly against Popper's falsificationism. Expository on a still-debated thesis (incommensurability remains contested). The counter's 'mob psychology' line is Lakatos's own phrase from his 1970 essay 'Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes', not from this SEP entry.

ev-epi-underdetermination.title: Underdetermination of Scientific Theory
ev-epi-underdetermination.strength: Authoritative scholarly entry (first published 2009, substantive revision 4 Apr 2023; fetch-verified). Develops confirmational (Duhem-Quine) holism, distinguishes it explicitly from contrastive underdetermination, and notes Duhem and Quine ran the two problems together; also covers the Laudan-Leplin (1991) reply. Expository on a debate where the strength of the threat is itself contested.

ev-epi-standpoint.title: Feminist Social Epistemology
ev-epi-standpoint.strength: Peer-reviewed scholarly entry; fetch-verified to cover Hartsock's Marxist-derived standpoint theory, Harding's 'strong objectivity' (examining the world from underprivileged positions), Haraway's 'situated knowledges', the epistemic-advantage thesis, the standpoint-as-'achieved stance' point, and named critics raising the relativism/internalized-oppression worries (Bar On 1993, Walby 2001, Nelson 1990). Longino's critical contextual empiricism and Haack's objectivity critique are documented in the linked SEP entries on feminist epistemology and feminist perspectives on science. Expository on a contested research programme; relativism objections are live.

ev-epi-justification.title: Foundationalist Theories of Epistemic Justification
ev-epi-justification.strength: Authoritative peer-reviewed encyclopedia entry on the regress problem and the foundationalism/coherentism response. The reliabilist alternative the card names is a distinct, well-established externalist position.

ev-poli-fptp.title: First-past-the-post voting
ev-poli-fptp.strength: Wikipedia 'First-past-the-post voting' supports the plurality rule (most first-preference votes wins without a majority), the spoiler effect, wasted votes (2005 UK: ~70% wasted), and the link to Duverger's law; the page also confirms the counter, noting most FPTP countries have multiparty legislatures, so Duverger's two-party result is a tendency with UK/India regional-party exceptions, a real opposing qualifier.

ev-poli-runoff.title: Two-round system
ev-poli-runoff.strength: Wikipedia 'Two-round system' supports the majority-then-top-two procedure, its use for the French presidency, and the 2002 first round (Chirac 19.9%, Le Pen 16.9%, Jospin 16.2% with the left vote divided); the page lists centre squeeze as a documented criticism of runoff rules but states Chirac was the majority-preferred candidate in 2002, so the card treats 2002 as vote-splitting rather than a clean centre squeeze. The Condorcet-based centre-squeeze critique is a real, documented opposing position.

ev-poli-rcv.title: Instant-runoff voting
ev-poli-rcv.strength: Wikipedia 'Instant-runoff voting' supports the rank-eliminate-transfer-until-majority procedure, the failure of monotonicity (ranking a candidate higher can make them lose), and the 2009 Burlington result where Bob Kiss defeated the majority-preferred Condorcet winner Andy Montroll, who was eliminated; the monotonicity and Condorcet criticism is a real, documented opposing position.

ev-poli-borda.title: Borda count
ev-poli-borda.strength: Wikipedia's 'Borda count' article documents the n-1, n-2, ... 0 point scheme, the summed-totals winner rule, and the method's vulnerability to teaming/cloning and to burying; it also records Borda's own quote ('My scheme is intended for only honest men'), a genuine acknowledgement by the method's author that it presumes sincere voting and fails under strategy, which is a real opposing position to relying on Borda for high-stakes votes.

ev-poli-condorcet.title: Condorcet paradox
ev-poli-condorcet.strength: Wikipedia's 'Condorcet paradox' article gives the definition of a Condorcet winner and the canonical 3-voter, 3-candidate cyclic example (A>B>C, B>C>A, C>A>B) producing A beats B, B beats C, C beats A each 2-to-1; the named counter, Borda's points method as a deliberate alternative to pairwise majorities, is a real historical opposing position from Condorcet's own contemporary.

ev-poli-approval.title: Approval voting
ev-poli-approval.strength: Wikipedia's 'Approval voting' article confirms the approve-any-number rule, the most-approvals-wins tally, and that the method reduces vote-splitting/spoilers (the Brams and Herschbach spoiler result); it references the Burr dilemma and cites Jack H. Nagel's 2007 Journal of Politics article 'The Burr Dilemma in Approval Voting' as its source, and it notes that the binary ballot ignores the expressive grades of rated methods, so both named limitations are genuine opposing positions rather than rhetorical 'critics say'.

ev-poli-stv.title: Single transferable vote
ev-poli-stv.strength: Wikipedia's STV article documents the Droop quota formula floor(votes/(seats+1))+1, surplus and elimination transfers, and the Ireland/Malta/Australian Senate usage; the counting-complexity, random-sample-transfer, and non-monotonicity criticisms it records are a real opposing position, with the Electoral Reform Society for STV and plurality defenders against it.

ev-poli-mmp.title: Mixed-member proportional representation
ev-poli-mmp.strength: Wikipedia's MMP article documents the two-vote design, compensatory list top-up so total seats match the party vote, and the German/New Zealand cases, plus overhang seats, the 5% threshold, and decoy-list tactics; Germany's 2023 abolition of overhang seats is a documented opposing response to the concern that MMP did not deliver clean proportionality.

ev-poli-gibbard.title: Gibbard–Satterthwaite theorem
ev-poli-gibbard.strength: Wikipedia's Gibbard-Satterthwaite article states the theorem (3+ outcomes, deterministic, non-dictatorial implies manipulable), its derivation from Arrow, and the determinism/rated-ballot/restricted-domain escape routes; the mechanism-design escape routes named by Gibbard and the practical-difficulty caveat are a real opposing qualification to treating manipulability as decisive.

ev-poli-may-theorem.title: May's theorem
ev-poli-may-theorem.strength: Wikipedia's 'May's theorem' states the unique-characterisation result (anonymity, neutrality, positive responsiveness) for two alternatives, attributed to Kenneth May 1952, and the corrected detail example illustrates positive responsiveness from a genuine 3-3 tie; the named counter, Arrow's impossibility theorem, is a real opposing result establishing that the guarantee fails for three or more options.

ev-poli-apportionment.title: Apportionment paradox
ev-poli-apportionment.strength: Wikipedia's 'Apportionment paradox' documents the Alabama paradox (1880 census, 8 seats at 299 vs 7 at 300) under largest-remainder and that divisor methods avoid it, and the D'Hondt and largest-remainder seat counts in the detail are recomputed correct; the named counter, the Balinski-Young theorem, is a real result proving no method can both follow quota and avoid the paradoxes, framing the D'Hondt versus Sainte-Lague trade-off as a genuine value choice.

ev-poli-gerrymander.title: Gerrymandering
ev-poli-gerrymander.strength: Wikipedia's 'Gerrymandering' defines packing and cracking and the efficiency gap (wasted votes = losing votes plus surplus above the winning threshold), citing Wisconsin's 2011 map and a federal ruling, plus independent commissions as responses, and the worked efficiency gap (199 vs 46, 30.6%) is recomputed correct; the named counter, Chief Justice Roberts writing the Rucho v. Common Cause (2019) majority, is a real opposing position holding partisan gerrymandering nonjusticiable in federal court, with the 'sociological gobbledygook' remark correctly attributed to his Gill v. Whitford argument rather than the Rucho opinion.

ev-poli-banzhaf.title: Banzhaf power index
ev-poli-banzhaf.strength: Wikipedia's 'Banzhaf power index' article defines the index as a player's share of swing (critical) memberships across winning coalitions and documents that power diverges from weight share, including dummy players with zero power (the Nassau County example, where Oyster Bay, Glen Cove, and Long Beach each had power 0). The article records that Lionel Penrose defined the measure in 1946 and John Banzhaf reinvented it in 1965 in the Nassau County malapportionment fight. The weights 50/49/1 at quota 51 yielding power 3/5, 1/5, 1/5, and the quiz case 3/2/2 at quota 4 yielding 1/3 each, were verified by direct enumeration. The named counter — Shapley and Shubik's order-of-arrival pivotality index, named in the same article as an accepted alternative measure of voting power — is a real and standard non-equivalent approach in the social-choice literature.

ev-bio-sir-model.title: Compartmental models in epidemiology
ev-bio-sir-model.strength: The Wikipedia article on compartmental models in epidemiology states the SIR equations, defines R0 = beta/gamma as the expected secondary cases in a fully susceptible population, gives the R0>1 grows / R0<1 dies out threshold, and confirms R0 is used to compute the herd-immunity vaccination threshold; the 1 - 1/R0 formula is the standard derivation from the susceptible share falling to 1/R0. The named counter is a real opposing position: epidemiologists in COVID-19 analyses argue R0 is context-dependent rather than a fixed pathogen constant, and structured/network models supersede the well-mixed SIR threshold.

ev-bio-hardy-weinberg.title: Hardy–Weinberg principle
ev-bio-hardy-weinberg.strength: The Wikipedia article on the Hardy-Weinberg principle states the genotype frequencies p^2, 2pq, q^2 under random mating, that they sum to 1, the list of forces (selection, mutation, migration/gene flow, drift, non-random mating) whose absence keeps them constant, and that deviation signals evolution (null-model framing). The named counter is real: G.H. Hardy treated the result as elementary, and population geneticists treat it strictly as a null hypothesis that finite real populations violate via drift and assortative mating.

ev-eco-lotka-volterra.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
ev-eco-lotka-volterra.strength: The Wikipedia article on the Lotka-Volterra equations gives the two coupled equations dx/dt = alpha*x - beta*x*y and dy/dt = -gamma*y + delta*x*y with each term's meaning, states the equilibrium at x = gamma/delta and y = alpha/beta, that the solutions are undamped periodic closed orbits with the predator trailing the prey by 90 degrees, and lists the unrealistic assumptions (prey have ample food at all times with no density limit, predators have limitless appetite). The named counter is a real opposing position: ecologists argue the neutral cycles are structurally fragile and that realistic models with carrying capacity and a Holling type-II functional response are needed, as in fits to the lynx-hare record.

ev-eco-logistic-map.title: Logistic map
ev-eco-logistic-map.strength: The Wikipedia 'Logistic map' article supports the equation x_next = r*x*(1-x), the fixed point 1-1/r for r<3, period-doubling past r=3, the onset of chaos near r=3.57, sensitive dependence on initial conditions, and Robert May's 1976 Nature paper as the origin; it also documents May's framing of the map as a teaching/modeling caution against literal forecasting, which is a real opposing emphasis to treating it as a population predictor.

ev-eco-species-area.title: Species–area relationship
ev-eco-species-area.strength: The Wikipedia 'Species-area relationship' article supports the form S = c*A^z, the typical z range of about 0.2 to 0.35, the log-log straight-line property of slope z, and its use in estimating extinctions from habitat loss; it also documents the He and Hubbell (2011) result that the species-area relationship overestimates extinction rates, a real published opposing position.

ev-geo-map-projection.title: Map projection
ev-geo-map-projection.strength: The Wikipedia 'Map projection' article supports the impossibility of preserving both angles and areas (tied to Gauss's theorema egregium), Mercator as conformal with pole-ward area inflation making Greenland look like Africa, Africa being roughly 14 times Greenland, and Gall-Peters as equal-area with shape distortion; it also documents the Peters controversy, where Arno Peters' political critique of Mercator was met by cartographers' rebuttal, a real named opposing exchange.

ev-ir-lanchester.title: Lanchester's laws
ev-ir-lanchester.strength: Wikipedia's 'Lanchester's laws' article states the square law (strength proportional to the square of unit count), gives the equations dA/dt = -bB, dB/dt = -aA, and the equal-firepower survivor formula sqrt(A^2 - B^2), plus the linear law for melee; sqrt(5^2-3^2)=4, sqrt(13^2-5^2)=12, and sqrt(100^2-70^2)=71.4 verified by direct computation. The counter (square law fails for guerrilla/asymmetric war, and omits terrain/morale/logistics) is a real, documented limitation discussed in the counterinsurgency literature.

ev-ir-richardson.title: Lewis Fry Richardson
ev-ir-richardson.strength: Wikipedia's 'Lewis Fry Richardson' article describes the coupled arms-race differential equations (arming proportional to rival's arms and to grievance, inversely to own arms), the stability-vs-runaway dependence on the coefficients, the base-10 log scaling of battle deaths giving a right-skewed Pareto (power-law) distribution of war sizes with wars-per-year Poisson, and his status as initiator of quantitative conflict analysis; the fatigue product 0.9*0.8=0.72 > 0.6*0.5=0.30 verified by computation. The counter (Hedley Bull's 1966 'classical approach' critique that formal models strip out politics and intentions) is a real, named opposing position in the IR methods debate.

ev-cyber-password-entropy.title: Password strength
ev-cyber-password-entropy.strength: Wikipedia's 'Password strength' article gives entropy as log2 of the number of possible passwords, the L*log2(N) formula, the worked figures (lowercase log2(26) about 4.7 bits per char; Diceware word lists of 7776 words giving about 12.9 bits per word), and the caveat that the formula assumes randomness while human-chosen passwords have far less; 10*log2(64)=60 and 5*log2(7776)=64.6 verified by computation. The counter (NIST SP 800-63B abandoning composition rules because the entropy model fails for human-chosen passwords) is a real, documented standards-body position.

ev-cyber-birthday-attack.title: Birthday attack
ev-cyber-birthday-attack.strength: Wikipedia's Birthday attack article states the 2^(l/2) collision bound, the ~1.25*sqrt(H) tries figure, lists MD5 as compromised, and ties the result to the birthday problem; the Schneier/community point that collision resistance is distinct from preimage resistance is a real, standard qualification of when the birthday bound applies.

ev-cs-pvsnp.title: P versus NP problem
ev-cs-pvsnp.strength: Wikipedia's P versus NP article confirms the P and NP definitions, the verify-versus-solve framing, NP-completeness, SAT as the first NP-complete problem, the Clay Millennium 1,000,000 dollar prize, the 88 percent (2018) belief in P != NP, and the cryptographic stakes; Knuth's stated lean toward a nonconstructive P = NP is a documented, named opposing position.

ev-cs-pagerank.title: PageRank
ev-cs-pagerank.strength: Wikipedia's PageRank article confirms the random-surfer/stationary-distribution interpretation, the dominant-eigenvector computation, the formula PR(A) = (1-d)/N + d*sum(PR(B)/L(B)), the 0.85 damping factor, and that PageRank is vulnerable to manipulation by link farms with Google countermeasures since 2007; the link-farm gameability is a real, documented limitation.

ev-philo-expected-utility.title: Expected utility hypothesis
ev-philo-expected-utility.strength: The Wikipedia 'Expected utility hypothesis' article supports the definition (probability-weighted sum of outcome utilities), the von Neumann-Morgenstern representation theorem and its four axioms, the St. Petersburg resolution via diminishing marginal utility (E[utility] = sum n/2^n = 2 utils under log2 utility), and documents the named opposing positions: Allais's paradox (independence violation) and Kahneman-Tversky prospect theory, both standard, replicated descriptive challenges to the normative theory.

ev-philo-dutch-book.title: Dutch book
ev-philo-dutch-book.strength: The Wikipedia 'Dutch book' article supports the construction (bets that jointly guarantee a loss when prices violate the probability axioms; 0.6+0.6 prices give a 0.2 euro sure loss), the conclusion that coherence forces credences to be probabilities, and the attribution to Ramsey and de Finetti. It also records the named limitation that the argument is widely read as a consistency norm rather than a literal threat, an opposing reading held by serious commentators including de Finetti himself.

ev-sys-centrality.title: Centrality
ev-sys-centrality.strength: The Wikipedia 'Centrality' article supports the definitions of degree, betweenness, and eigenvector centrality, the point that they capture distinct notions of importance and can rank nodes differently, and the bridge-node intuition for betweenness (bridge with degree 2 but highest betweenness over 3 times 3 = 9 cross-cluster pairs). The named counter (Borgatti's argument that each centrality presupposes a specific flow process, so measure choice must match the real diffusion mechanism) is a documented position in the network-science literature.

ev-prob-markov-chain.title: Markov chain
ev-prob-markov-chain.strength: Wikipedia's 'Markov chain' article states the memoryless property, the transition matrix and distribution multiplication, and that an irreducible aperiodic chain has a unique stationary distribution equal to a left eigenvector with eigenvalue 1, supporting the worked weather example (0.1*P(sunny)=0.5*P(rainy) gives 5/6 and 1/6). The named limitation is real: the convergence theorem genuinely requires irreducibility and aperiodicity, and higher-order and hidden-Markov models exist precisely because the first-order memoryless assumption fails for many real series.

ev-prob-monte-carlo.title: Monte Carlo method
ev-prob-monte-carlo.strength: Wikipedia's 'Monte Carlo method' article states that the method uses repeated random sampling, gives the inscribed-quadrant pi example with ratio pi/4, states 1/sqrt(N) convergence (quadrupling samples halves error), and lists finance, physics, and risk applications, supporting the worked example (1500/2000=0.75, times 4 = 3; tenfold error cut needs 100x samples). The named limitation is real: deterministic quadrature genuinely beats Monte Carlo for smooth low-dimensional integrals, and dependence on random-number quality is a recognized failure mode addressed by quasi-Monte Carlo.

ev-prob-power-law.title: Power law
ev-prob-power-law.strength: Wikipedia's 'Power law' article states the form p(x) = C x^(-a), names the log-log straight line as the signature (slope -a), lists Zipf word frequency, city sizes, and income/Pareto as examples, and notes power laws permit black-swan behavior unlike the bell curve, supporting the worked Zipf example (top word 6000, 3rd around 2000; 9000 to 3000 in the quiz). The named counter is real: Clauset, Shalizi, and Newman's 2009 SIAM Review paper showed many empirical power-law claims do not survive rigorous goodness-of-fit testing against alternatives like the log-normal.

ev-game-shapley.title: Shapley value
ev-game-shapley.strength: The Wikipedia 'Shapley value' article supports the average-marginal-contribution definition, the four characterizing axioms (efficiency, symmetry, dummy/null, additivity/linearity), the glove-game numbers, and the cost-sharing and SHAP applications; the named counter (nucleolus/core and Roth's stability critique) is a real, standard alternative solution concept in cooperative game theory.

ev-echist-malthus.title: Malthusian growth model
ev-echist-malthus.strength: The Wikipedia 'Malthusian growth model' article supports the 1798 essay, the geometric-population versus arithmetic-food claim, the exponential-overtakes-linear math, and the checks on growth; the named counter (Ester Boserup, 'The Conditions of Agricultural Growth', 1965) is a real and widely cited opposing position in economic history.

ev-hist-radiocarbon.title: Radiocarbon dating
ev-hist-radiocarbon.strength: The Wikipedia 'Radiocarbon dating' article supports the ~5,730-year half-life, the halving-with-each-half-life math, the ~50,000-year practical limit, the need for calibration because atmospheric C-14 varied, and Libby's development of the method; the named counter (Hessel de Vries and the de Vries effect showing non-constant atmospheric C-14) is a real, documented finding that established the necessity of calibration.

ev-prob-benford.title: Benford's law
ev-prob-benford.strength: Wikipedia's Benford's law article supports the formula P(d)=log10(1+1/d), the ~30%/~18%/<5% leading-digit frequencies (computed: P(1)=30.1, P(2)=17.6, P(9)=4.58, P(4)=9.69), the scale-invariance derivation, the orders-of-magnitude caveat, and forensic use; Walter Mebane is a real opposing/qualifying authority who originated Benford election forensics yet publicly rejected the 2020 precinct-level application as misuse.

ev-prob-birthday.title: Birthday problem
ev-prob-birthday.strength: Wikipedia's Birthday problem article supports the 23-person ~50.7% figure (computed 50.73%, complement product 0.4927), the 253 pairs (23*22/2) and 435 pairs (30*29/2), the complement formula, the 99.9% at 70 people (computed 99.92%), and the sqrt(N)/2^(N/2) scaling tied to birthday attacks; Xiaoyun Wang's 2004 MD5 and 2005 SHA-1 collision attacks are a real, documented exploitation of that same scaling and stand as the concrete adversarial counterpart.

ev-pe-platform-capitalism.who: Nick Srnicek; Shoshana Zuboff; Jean Tirole
ev-pe-platform-capitalism.title: Platform Capitalism / The Age of Surveillance Capitalism / Nobel lecture on two-sided markets
ev-pe-platform-capitalism.where: Polity Press; PublicAffairs; American Economic Review
ev-pe-platform-capitalism.strength: Srnicek's 2017 taxonomy of five platform types is a widely-cited academic framework; Zuboff's 2019 book is peer-reviewed and the source of 'behavioural futures markets'; Tirole's Nobel-lecture analysis of two-sided markets (2014 prize) is the authoritative economic treatment. Combined coverage of both the political-economy and market-design dimensions is broad.

ev-pe-varoufakis-technofeudalism.title: Technofeudalism: What Killed Capitalism
ev-pe-varoufakis-technofeudalism.strength: Single authored book by a professional economist and former finance minister; primary source for all Varoufakis-attributed claims. Cloud capital, cloudalist, vassal capitalist and cloud serf are Varoufakis's own coinage. Commission-rate figures (Apple 30%, Amazon 35%+) are publicly documented in platform terms of service and confirmed in Congressional and EC antitrust hearings.

ev-pe-thelen-varieties-platform.title: Regulating Uber: The Politics of the Platform Economy in Europe and the United States
ev-pe-thelen-varieties-platform.strength: Peer-reviewed article in a leading political science journal by MIT political scientist Kathleen Thelen. The VoC framework (deregulation / dualism / embedded flexibility) is from her 2014 Cambridge University Press book 'Varieties of Liberalization'. Uber case studies in US/Europe are documented from regulatory decisions and news sources cited in the article.

ev-pe-cloud-rent.who: Jean Tirole; Varoufakis; Tobias Adrian & Hyun Song Shin
ev-pe-cloud-rent.title: Cloud rent, data portability and digital market regulation
ev-pe-cloud-rent.where: Multiple: Tirole (2014 Nobel lecture); AWS 2023 10-K SEC filing; Adrian & Shin (2014 BIS paper)
ev-pe-cloud-rent.strength: AWS operating margin from 2023 annual SEC filing (verified public company disclosure). Tirole's data portability argument from his 2014 Nobel lecture and subsequent regulatory commentary. The three rent categories (access, data, infrastructure) synthesise Varoufakis and Srnicek frameworks.

ev-cn-sez.title: How Asia Works; Shenzhen Special Economic Zone development record
ev-cn-sez.where: Profile Books; World Bank development reports
ev-cn-sez.strength: Studwell's 'How Asia Works' (2013) is the standard treatment of export discipline and SEZ logic; Shenzhen population figures (1979: ~30,000; 2020: 12+ million) are from PRC census data. 1980 SEZ designation and 1984 14-city opening are documented official policy events.

ev-cn-pboc.title: China's monetary and exchange rate policy
ev-cn-pboc.where: IMF Article IV consultations; US Treasury currency reports; Prasad 'The Dollar Trap' (2014)
ev-cn-pboc.strength: IMF Article IV consultation reports are authoritative public documents on PBoC operations. RMB SDR inclusion in 2015 is documented official IMF decision. US Treasury 'currency manipulator' designations (2019, reversed 2020) are official public records. Reserve figures from SAFE official publications.

ev-cn-made-in-china-2025.who: State Council of China; Scott Kennedy (CSIS)
ev-cn-made-in-china-2025.title: Made in China 2025 (中国制造2025); CSIS analysis
ev-cn-made-in-china-2025.where: State Council document May 2015; CSIS Critical Questions June 2015
ev-cn-made-in-china-2025.strength: Primary source is the official State Council document (authenticated; CSIS and EU Chamber of Commerce translations widely cited). Ten target sectors are explicitly listed in the original document. Section 301 investigation (2017) and CHIPS Act (2022) are official US government actions with public legislative text.

ev-cn-dual-circulation.who: Xi Jinping; Michael Pettis; Arthur Kroeber
ev-cn-dual-circulation.title: Dual circulation strategy; China's Economy (Kroeber)
ev-cn-dual-circulation.where: Xinhua official announcement May 2020; 14th Five Year Plan; Pettis via Carnegie Endowment
ev-cn-dual-circulation.strength: Dual circulation coined by Xi Jinping in official speech (Xinhua, May 14 2020) and formalised in 14th Five-Year Plan (March 2021, official text). China household consumption share ~38% is from World Bank national accounts data. Michael Pettis's argument about suppressed wages/deposit rates is published in Carnegie Endowment working papers.

ev-cn-financial-repression.who: Ronald McKinnon; Edward Shaw; World Bank; Michael Pettis
ev-cn-financial-repression.title: Money and Capital in Economic Development; World Bank China financial repression estimates
ev-cn-financial-repression.where: Brookings Institution Press (McKinnon 1973); World Bank Policy Research Working Paper
ev-cn-financial-repression.strength: McKinnon 'Money and Capital' (1973) and Shaw 'Financial Deepening' (1973) are the original academic sources for the term; both Stanford economists published in the same year. World Bank 4% of GDP subsidy estimate is from official research reports (Lardy and others). US Regulation Q history is documented fact.

ev-vn-doi-moi.who: World Bank; Vietnam GSO; Adam Fforde and Stefan de Vylder
ev-vn-doi-moi.title: Vietnam: Joining the World; From Plan to Market
ev-vn-doi-moi.where: World Bank Vietnam country overview; Westview Press (Fforde & de Vylder)
ev-vn-doi-moi.strength: World Bank lower-middle income reclassification (2009) is an official Bank designation. Vietnam 1986 inflation (700%+) and Khoán 10 (1988) are documented in Vietnamese government and World Bank records. GDP growth average over 7% from 1990–2019 is from World Bank WDI data. Sixth National Congress date (December 1986) is official PVN historical record.

ev-vn-export-led.title: Vietnam manufacturing export data; Rodrik on premature deindustrialisation
ev-vn-export-led.where: World Bank WDI; UNCTAD trade statistics; Rodrik (2016) Journal of Economic Growth
ev-vn-export-led.strength: Samsung's ~20% share of Vietnam exports is documented in MoIT Vietnam statistics and Samsung annual reports. Vietnam's second-largest garment/footwear export rank is from WTO trade statistics. Rodrik's 'premature deindustrialisation' concept is from peer-reviewed article in Journal of Economic Growth (2016).

ev-vn-monetary.who: State Bank of Vietnam; US Treasury; IMF
ev-vn-monetary.title: SBV exchange rate policy; US Treasury currency report December 2020
ev-vn-monetary.where: SBV official publications; US Treasury semi-annual currency report
ev-vn-monetary.strength: Currency manipulator designation (December 2020) and reversal (April 2021) are official US Treasury actions with public documentation. De-dollarisation programme details (2012 SBV directives) are official regulatory documents. Dollarisation share >30% in 1990s and <10% by 2020 are from SBV official statistics cited in IMF Article IV consultations.

ev-sg-edb.who: EDB Singapore; Goh Keng Swee; Joe Studwell
ev-sg-edb.title: Economic Development Board history; Singapore industrial policy
ev-sg-edb.where: EDB official history; Goh Keng Swee collected writings; Studwell 'How Asia Works'
ev-sg-edb.strength: EDB founding (1961) and phase-based upgrading strategy are documented in official EDB publications and confirmed in multiple academic studies of Singapore's development (Huff 1994, Low 1998). Goh Keng Swee's rejection of import substitution is from his own published writings. Temasek portfolio companies are public information. Singapore independence date (1965) is a historical fact.

ev-sg-mas-neer.title: MAS monetary policy framework
ev-sg-mas-neer.where: MAS official policy statements; MAS Macroeconomic Review
ev-sg-mas-neer.strength: MAS NEER policy framework is directly documented on MAS's own website and in its semi-annual Macroeconomic Review. Three parameters (slope, width, centre) are explicitly described in official MAS communications. MAS founding year 1971 is a historical fact. Average CPI ~2% 1990–2020 is from Singapore DOS official data.

ev-sg-cpf.title: CPF Annual Report; Singapore housing statistics
ev-sg-cpf.where: CPF Board official reports; HDB annual report
ev-sg-cpf.strength: CPF contribution rates (37% combined under 55) are published on CPF Board's official website. HDB 80% population share and ~90% homeownership rate are from HDB annual report 2022. CPF founding 1955 is historical fact. GIC as long-term reserve manager is documented on GIC and MAS official sites. Counter-cyclical rate cuts (1986, 1998, 2003) are documented in Singapore government budget statements.

ev-west-volcker-shock.title: Keeping At It: The Quest for Sound Money and Good Government
ev-west-volcker-shock.strength: Federal funds rate peak (~20% June 1981) and unemployment peak (10.8% December 1982) are from Federal Reserve FRED database (official Fed data). Mexico 1982 default is a documented historical event. Volcker's October 1979 reserve-targeting shift is confirmed in Fed historical records. Inflation drop 14.8% (1980) to 3.2% (1983) from Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI data.

ev-west-inflation-targeting.who: Ben Bernanke; Reserve Bank of New Zealand; Finn Kydland & Edward Prescott
ev-west-inflation-targeting.title: Inflation targeting; Rules rather than discretion: The inconsistency of optimal plans
ev-west-inflation-targeting.where: RBNZ Act 1989; Journal of Political Economy (Kydland & Prescott 1977); Fed 2012 statement
ev-west-inflation-targeting.strength: RBNZ adoption of IT in 1990 is documented in the RBNZ Act 1989 and subsequent policy implementation. Kydland-Prescott (1977) is a Nobel Prize-winning paper in Journal of Political Economy. Fed's formal 2% target statement (January 25, 2012) is public record. US/UK 9% inflation in 2022 from official BLS/ONS data.

ev-west-qe.who: Federal Reserve; Tobias Adrian & Hyun Song Shin
ev-west-qe.title: Federal Reserve QE programmes; Procyclical Leverage and Endogenous Risk
ev-west-qe.where: Federal Reserve press releases; BIS Working Paper (Adrian & Shin)
ev-west-qe.strength: Fed balance sheet figures ($900bn pre-2008, $4.5tn 2015, $9tn 2022) from Federal Reserve H.4.1 statistical releases (official data). QE programme dates from official Fed press releases. '2013 taper tantrum' is documented in Fed FOMC minutes and IMF reports. Adrian & Shin BIS paper is peer-reviewed.

ev-west-post-covid-indpol.who: Mariana Mazzucato; US Congress; European Commission
ev-west-post-covid-indpol.title: The Entrepreneurial State; CHIPS and Science Act; Inflation Reduction Act; EU Green Deal Industrial Plan
ev-west-post-covid-indpol.where: Anthem Press (Mazzucato 2013); Public Law 117-167 (CHIPS Act); Public Law 117-169 (IRA); EC COM(2023) 62
ev-west-post-covid-indpol.strength: CHIPS Act ($280bn) and IRA ($369bn) are official US legislation with confirmed spending figures from Congressional Budget Office. EU Chips Act (€43bn) is official EC regulation. Mazzucato's DARPA/internet argument is documented in her 2013 book with verifiable primary sources. IRA domestic-content requirements and EU friction are documented in EC and USTR official communications.

ev-west-indpol-debate.who: Dani Rodrik; Paul Krugman; James Brander; Daron Acemoglu; James Robinson
ev-west-indpol-debate.title: Green Industrial Policy; Strategic Trade Policy and the New International Economics; Why Nations Fail
ev-west-indpol-debate.where: Oxford Review of Economic Policy (Rodrik); MIT Press (Krugman ed.); Crown Publishers (Acemoglu & Robinson)
ev-west-indpol-debate.strength: Rodrik's 'Green Industrial Policy' article in Oxford Review of Economic Policy (2014) is peer-reviewed and is the source of the market-failure targeting framework. Krugman's strategic trade theory appears in his edited 1986 MIT Press volume. Acemoglu-Robinson critique of developmental state generalisability comes from 'Why Nations Fail' (2012, widely reviewed). Kydland-Prescott knowledge-problem argument is Nobel-winning.

ev-poli-marxism-ideology.title: The Communist Manifesto; The Open Society and Its Enemies
ev-poli-marxism-ideology.strength: The Communist Manifesto (1848) is a primary source, freely available and multiply verified. The 'executive committee of the bourgeoisie' quote is verbatim from Section I. Popper's 'historicism' critique is from *The Open Society and Its Enemies* Vol. 2, Chapter 13. Bernstein revisionism quote ('The goal is nothing, the movement is everything') is from *Evolutionary Socialism* Ch. 5.

ev-poli-leninism.title: What Is to Be Done?; Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism; The Russian Revolution (Luxemburg)
ev-poli-leninism.where: Iskra Press (1902); Zhizn i Znanie (1917); Paul Levi (1922, Luxemburg posthumous)
ev-poli-leninism.strength: Primary sources: Lenin's *What Is to Be Done?* (1902) and *Imperialism* (1916) are both available in verified Collected Works editions. Constituent Assembly dissolution (January 1918) is a documented historical event in Soviet records. Luxemburg's *The Russian Revolution* is her posthumously published critique, written 1918.

ev-poli-stalinism.title: The Origins of Totalitarianism; The Great Terror; History of the Communist Party (Short Course)
ev-poli-stalinism.strength: Arendt's totalitarianism framework is peer-reviewed and widely taught. Gulag death estimates vary widely in scholarship (1.5–18m range reflects genuine historical uncertainty between Conquest's higher and Getty/Rittersporn lower estimates). Holodomor death estimates (3.5–7m) reflect current Ukrainian government and academic consensus range. The Short Course authorship is established historical fact.

ev-poli-trotskyism.who: Leon Trotsky; Tony Cliff; Milovan Đilas
ev-poli-trotskyism.title: The Revolution Betrayed; State Capitalism in Russia (Cliff); The New Class (Đilas)
ev-poli-trotskyism.where: Doubleday (1937, English tr.); Bookmarks (Cliff); Thames & Hudson (Đilas, 1957)
ev-poli-trotskyism.strength: Trotsky's *The Revolution Betrayed* (1936) is a primary source. The degenerated workers' state / state capitalism / bureaucratic collectivism debate is well-documented in Trotskyist and socialist historiography. Trotsky's assassination (August 1940, Ramón Mercader) is confirmed by Mexican judicial records and subsequent Soviet archive revelations.

ev-poli-maoism.title: On the Mass Line; Mao's Great Famine (Dikötter)
ev-poli-maoism.where: Selected Works of Mao Tse-tung Vol. 3; Bloomsbury (Dikötter, 2010)
ev-poli-maoism.strength: Mao's 'On the Mass Line' (1943) is from the verified Collected Works. Cultural Revolution death estimates (500k–2m) are from mainstream academic range; Dikötter's Great Leap Forward estimates (45m+) are higher end of scholarly debate. The Sino-Soviet split (1960) is documented in Soviet and Chinese archives now partially open.

ev-poli-anarchism.who: Peter Kropotkin; Mikhail Bakunin; Emma Goldman
ev-poli-anarchism.title: Mutual Aid: A Factor of Evolution; God and the State (Bakunin); Living My Life (Goldman)
ev-poli-anarchism.strength: Kropotkin's *Mutual Aid* (1902) is a primary source, freely available. Bakunin's expulsion from the First International (1872) is a documented historical event. The CNT-FAI collectivisation in Catalonia (1936–39) is documented in Spanish Civil War historiography (George Orwell's *Homage to Catalonia*, Gerald Brenan's *The Spanish Labyrinth*).

ev-poli-social-democracy-ideology.who: Eduard Bernstein; Rosa Luxemburg; Wolfgang Streeck
ev-poli-social-democracy-ideology.title: Evolutionary Socialism; Reform or Revolution; Buying Time
ev-poli-social-democracy-ideology.where: Swan Sonnenschein (Bernstein, 1909 English tr.); Bookmarks (Luxemburg); Verso (Streeck, 2014)
ev-poli-social-democracy-ideology.strength: Bernstein's *Evolutionary Socialism* and Luxemburg's *Reform or Revolution* are primary sources. Clause IV removal (1995) is documented UK Labour Party history. Beveridge Report (1942) and NHS founding (1948) are verified historical events. Streeck's *Buying Time* (2013) is a peer-reviewed political economy work.

ev-poli-classical-liberalism.who: John Locke; J.S. Mill; Isaiah Berlin; C.B. Macpherson
ev-poli-classical-liberalism.title: Two Treatises of Government; On Liberty; Two Concepts of Liberty; The Political Theory of Possessive Individualism
ev-poli-classical-liberalism.where: Awnsham Churchill (Locke, 1689); Parker (Mill, 1859); Clarendon Press (Berlin, 1958); Oxford UP (Macpherson, 1962)
ev-poli-classical-liberalism.strength: All cited texts are canonical primary and secondary sources. Mill's harm principle is verbatim from *On Liberty* Chapter 1. Berlin's negative/positive liberty distinction is from the 1958 Oxford inaugural lecture, published by Clarendon Press. Jefferson's Lockean debt (Declaration of Independence) is historically established.

ev-poli-conservatism.who: Edmund Burke; Michael Oakeshott; Roger Scruton
ev-poli-conservatism.title: Reflections on the Revolution in France; Rationalism in Politics; The Meaning of Conservatism
ev-poli-conservatism.strength: Burke's *Reflections* is a primary source (1790); 'partnership between the dead, the living and those yet to be born' is verbatim. Oakeshott's 'disposition' characterisation is from *Rationalism in Politics* Ch. 8. Scruton's 'trust' argument is from *The Meaning of Conservatism* and *How to Be a Conservative* (2014).

ev-poli-fascism.title: The Nature of Fascism; The Anatomy of Fascism
ev-poli-fascism.strength: Griffin's 'palingenetic ultranationalism' definition is from *The Nature of Fascism* (1991), peer-reviewed and now the dominant academic definition. Paxton's *The Anatomy of Fascism* (2004) is the leading historical account. March on Rome (October 1922) appointment by Victor Emmanuel III is a documented historical event. Italian racial laws (1938) are documented official state acts.

ev-poli-nazism.who: Hannah Arendt; Saul Friedländer; Ian Kershaw
ev-poli-nazism.title: The Origins of Totalitarianism; Nazi Germany and the Jews; Hitler (biography)
ev-poli-nazism.strength: Arendt's totalitarianism analysis and 'banality of evil' concept are from published, peer-reviewed books. Holocaust death toll (~6m Jews, ~5-6m others) is established by Yad Vashem and Holocaust historiography consensus. Article 48 of the Weimar Constitution is a documented historical provision. Friedländer's 'redemptive antisemitism' is from his two-volume Pulitzer Prize-winning history.

ev-poli-neoliberalism-ideology.who: Friedrich Hayek; Michel Foucault; Quinn Slobodian
ev-poli-neoliberalism-ideology.title: The Road to Serfdom; Birth of Biopolitics (lectures); Globalists
ev-poli-neoliberalism-ideology.where: Routledge (Hayek, 1944); Seuil/Gallimard (Foucault, lectures 1978-79, pub. 2004); Harvard UP (Slobodian, 2018)
ev-poli-neoliberalism-ideology.strength: Hayek's *Road to Serfdom* (1944) is a primary source. Foucault's *Birth of Biopolitics* lectures (1978–79, published 2004) are the source of the governmental/human-capital analysis. Mont Pelerin Society founding (1947) is documented historical fact. Slobodian's *Globalists* (2018, Harvard UP) is peer-reviewed and widely cited.

ev-poli-libertarianism.title: Anarchy, State, and Utopia; Self-Ownership, Freedom and Equality
ev-poli-libertarianism.strength: Nozick's *Anarchy, State, and Utopia* (1974) is the canonical primary text of libertarian philosophy; all attributed claims are from it. G.A. Cohen's *Self-Ownership, Freedom and Equality* (1995) is the standard philosophical rebuttal. Both are peer-reviewed academic publications.

ev-poli-rousseau.title: The Social Contract
ev-poli-rousseau.strength: Primary text (Du contrat social, 1762); SEP article surveys secondary literature across political philosophy.

ev-poli-hegel-state.title: Elements of the Philosophy of Right
ev-poli-hegel-state.strength: Primary text (Grundlinien der Philosophie des Rechts, 1820); SEP survey of Hegel's political philosophy.

ev-poli-habermas.title: Between Facts and Norms
ev-poli-habermas.strength: Primary text (Faktizität und Geltung, 1992); SEP entry covers deliberative democracy and discourse ethics.

ev-poli-pettit-republicanism.title: Republicanism: A Theory of Freedom and Government
ev-poli-pettit-republicanism.strength: Primary text; SEP entry on republicanism covers Pettit, Skinner, and the non-domination tradition.

ev-poli-tocqueville.title: Democracy in America
ev-poli-tocqueville.strength: Primary text (De la démocratie en Amérique, 1835–40); SEP entry surveys Tocqueville's political sociology.

ev-poli-weber-state.title: Politics as a Vocation
ev-poli-weber-state.strength: Primary text (Politik als Beruf, 1919); SEP surveys Weber's sociology of domination and the state.

ev-poli-tilly.title: Coercion, Capital, and European States, AD 990–1992
ev-poli-tilly.strength: Primary text: systematic comparative history of European state formation; widely cited in comparative politics.

ev-poli-lipset-rokkan.who: Seymour Martin Lipset and Stein Rokkan
ev-poli-lipset-rokkan.title: Party Systems and Voter Alignments
ev-poli-lipset-rokkan.strength: Foundational essay in comparative politics; cleavage theory widely taught and tested across party-system studies.

ev-poli-odonnell-schmitter.title: Transitions from Authoritarian Rule: Tentative Conclusions about Uncertain Democracies
ev-poli-odonnell-schmitter.strength: Canonical text of transitology; shaped all subsequent democratization scholarship.

ev-poli-linz-presidentialism.title: The Perils of Presidentialism
ev-poli-linz-presidentialism.strength: Highly cited article in Journal of Democracy; generated a sustained comparative-institutions debate.

ev-poli-levitsky-ziblatt.title: How Democracies Die
ev-poli-levitsky-ziblatt.strength: Widely reviewed bestseller drawing on systematic comparative analysis of democratic decline.

ev-poli-mill-methods.title: A System of Logic
ev-poli-mill-methods.strength: Primary text (1843); Mill's canons of induction remain the foundational exposition of comparative causal logic.

ev-poli-process-tracing.who: Andrew Bennett and Jeffrey T. Checkel (eds.)
ev-poli-process-tracing.title: Process Tracing: From Metaphor to Analytic Tool
ev-poli-process-tracing.strength: Standard methodological reference for qualitative causal inference in political science.

ev-poli-gramsci.title: Selections from the Prison Notebooks
ev-poli-gramsci.strength: Primary texts (written 1929–35, published posthumously); SEP entry covers hegemony and political philosophy.

ev-poli-bourdieu-field.title: Language and Symbolic Power
ev-poli-bourdieu-field.strength: Primary source for political field theory; Wikipedia entry cross-references La distinction and field theory.

ev-poli-seat-vote.title: The Relationship Between Seats and Votes in Two-Party Systems
ev-poli-seat-vote.where: Wikipedia — Cube root law of assembly sizes
ev-poli-seat-vote.strength: Classic empirical finding; disproportionality of FPTP seat-vote curve is well-replicated across democracies.

ev-poli-cartel-parties.title: Changing Models of Party Organization and Party Democracy: The Emergence of the Cartel Party
ev-poli-cartel-parties.strength: Influential Party Politics article; cartel party concept widely cited in comparative party systems literature.

ev-poli-lijphart.title: Democracy in Plural Societies
ev-poli-lijphart.strength: Founding text of consociational theory; Lijphart's cross-national comparisons are widely cited.

ev-poli-state-capacity.title: State-Building: Governance and World Order in the 21st Century
ev-poli-state-capacity.strength: Wikipedia entry synthesises the comparative-politics and development-economics literatures on state capacity.

ev-poli-path-dependence.title: Politics in Time: History, Institutions, and Social Analysis
ev-poli-path-dependence.strength: Pierson's text is the standard reference for path dependence in political science; Wikipedia entry covers QWERTY and welfare state examples.

ev-poli-republican-integration.title: La République et sa diversité
ev-poli-republican-integration.strength: Wikipedia entry summarises the scholarly debate on French republican universalism and its critics.

ev-philo-frege.title: Sense and Reference (Über Sinn und Bedeutung)
ev-philo-frege.strength: Primary text; founding paper of analytic philosophy of language.

ev-philo-russell-descriptions.title: On Denoting
ev-philo-russell-descriptions.strength: Primary text; one of the most discussed papers in 20th-century analytic philosophy.

ev-philo-wittgenstein-tractatus.title: Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus
ev-philo-wittgenstein-tractatus.strength: Primary text; SEP entry covers both early and late Wittgenstein comprehensively.

ev-philo-wittgenstein-pi.title: Philosophical Investigations
ev-philo-wittgenstein-pi.strength: Primary text; one of the two most influential works in 20th-century analytic philosophy.

ev-philo-austin.title: How to Do Things with Words
ev-philo-austin.where: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Speech Acts
ev-philo-austin.strength: Primary text; SEP entry on speech acts covers Austin, Searle, and Grice.

ev-philo-grice.title: Logic and Conversation
ev-philo-grice.strength: Primary text; SEP entry on implicature surveys Gricean pragmatics thoroughly.

ev-philo-kripke.title: Naming and Necessity
ev-philo-kripke.where: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Rigid Designators
ev-philo-kripke.strength: Primary text; SEP entry on rigid designators covers Kripke's innovations thoroughly.

ev-philo-kant-ethics.title: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals
ev-philo-kant-ethics.where: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Kant's Moral Philosophy
ev-philo-kant-ethics.strength: Primary text; SEP entry is the standard secondary reference for Kant's ethics.

ev-philo-mill-ethics.title: Utilitarianism
ev-philo-mill-ethics.strength: Primary text; SEP entry covers both the utilitarian theory and harm principle.

ev-philo-aristotle-ethics.title: Nicomachean Ethics
ev-philo-aristotle-ethics.where: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Aristotle's Ethics
ev-philo-aristotle-ethics.strength: Primary text; SEP entry is the authoritative secondary source on Aristotelian ethics.

ev-philo-macintyre.title: After Virtue
ev-philo-macintyre.where: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Alasdair MacIntyre
ev-philo-macintyre.strength: Highly influential neo-Aristotelian critique of modern ethics; SEP entry provides scholarly context.

ev-philo-scanlon.title: What We Owe to Each Other
ev-philo-scanlon.strength: Primary text; SEP entry on contractualism situates Scanlon against Rawls and Kant.

ev-philo-singer.title: Famine, Affluence, and Morality
ev-philo-singer.where: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Peter Singer
ev-philo-singer.strength: Highly cited paper; SEP entry surveys Singer's utilitarian and effective altruism arguments.

ev-philo-parfit.title: Reasons and Persons
ev-philo-parfit.where: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Derek Parfit
ev-philo-parfit.strength: Major text in analytic ethics; SEP entry covers personal identity and population ethics.

ev-philo-descartes.title: Meditations on First Philosophy
ev-philo-descartes.strength: Primary text; SEP entry is the canonical secondary source on Cartesian dualism.

ev-philo-functionalism.title: Psychological Predicates
ev-philo-functionalism.strength: Founding paper of functionalism; SEP entry surveys the functionalism debate exhaustively.

ev-philo-searle.title: Minds, Brains, and Programs
ev-philo-searle.where: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Chinese Room Argument
ev-philo-searle.strength: Highly cited paper; SEP entry on the Chinese room is comprehensive and presents all major replies.

ev-philo-chalmers.title: Facing Up to the Problem of Consciousness
ev-philo-chalmers.strength: Highly cited paper that coined 'the hard problem'; SEP entry surveys the consciousness debate.

ev-philo-nagel.title: What Is It Like to Be a Bat?
ev-philo-nagel.where: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Thomas Nagel
ev-philo-nagel.strength: One of the most-read philosophy papers; SEP entry covers Nagel's philosophy of mind.

ev-philo-universals.title: Universals and Scientific Realism
ev-philo-universals.strength: SEP entries on universals and medieval universals cover realism, nominalism, and conceptualism.

ev-philo-possible-worlds.title: On the Plurality of Worlds
ev-philo-possible-worlds.where: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Possible Worlds
ev-philo-possible-worlds.strength: Primary text for modal realism; SEP entry surveys all versions of possible worlds semantics.

ev-philo-lewis-causation.title: Causation
ev-philo-lewis-causation.where: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Counterfactual Theories of Causation
ev-philo-lewis-causation.strength: Founding paper of counterfactual causation; SEP entry covers the full debate.

ev-philo-personal-identity.title: Reasons and Persons (Part III)
ev-philo-personal-identity.where: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Personal Identity
ev-philo-personal-identity.strength: SEP entry is the best survey of the personal identity debate from Locke through Parfit.

ev-philo-lakatos.title: The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes
ev-philo-lakatos.strength: Primary text; SEP entry situates Lakatos between Popper and Kuhn.

ev-philo-feyerabend.title: Against Method
ev-philo-feyerabend.strength: Primary text; SEP entry covers the epistemological anarchism thesis.

ev-hist-athenian-democracy.title: Athenian democracy
ev-hist-athenian-democracy.strength: Encyclopaedic synthesis citing ancient sources (Thucydides, Aristotle) and modern classical scholarship.

ev-hist-persian-wars.title: Greco-Persian Wars
ev-hist-persian-wars.strength: Encyclopaedic account drawing on Herodotus, Thucydides, and modern archaeology.

ev-hist-roman-republic.title: Roman Republic
ev-hist-roman-republic.strength: Encyclopaedic account citing Polybius, Livy, and modern Roman historians.

ev-hist-roman-empire.title: Roman Empire
ev-hist-roman-empire.strength: Comprehensive encyclopaedic article on the Imperial period.

ev-hist-fall-rome.title: The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
ev-hist-fall-rome.where: Wikipedia — Fall of the Western Roman Empire
ev-hist-fall-rome.strength: Wikipedia article synthesises Gibbon and subsequent historiography; the fall of Rome is among the most debated historical events.

ev-hist-silk-roads.title: Silk Road
ev-hist-silk-roads.strength: Encyclopaedic account drawing on archaeological and textual evidence.

ev-hist-feudalism.title: Feudalism
ev-hist-feudalism.strength: Encyclopaedic account synthesising the long historiographical debate over feudalism as a concept.

ev-hist-islamic-golden-age.title: Islamic Golden Age
ev-hist-islamic-golden-age.strength: Encyclopaedic article drawing on history of science and Islamic studies literature.

ev-hist-mongols.title: Mongol Empire
ev-hist-mongols.strength: Encyclopaedic account citing David Morgan, Timothy May, and other Mongolia scholars.

ev-hist-hundred-years-war.title: Hundred Years' War
ev-hist-hundred-years-war.strength: Encyclopaedic account drawing on medieval chronicles and modern scholarship.

ev-hist-renaissance.title: Renaissance

ev-behav-hyperbolic.title: Hyperbolic discounting

ev-deveco-institutions.title: Why Nations Fail

ev-deveco-modernisation.title: Modernization theory
ev-deveco-modernisation.strength: Wikipedia covers Rostow's stages of growth and modernisation theory; standard reference.

ev-deveco-poverty-traps.title: Poverty trap
ev-deveco-poverty-traps.strength: Wikipedia article on poverty traps, big push models, and Sachs's approach.

ev-deveco-colonial-legacy.title: The Colonial Origins of Comparative Development
ev-deveco-colonial-legacy.strength: Highly cited AER paper using settler mortality as IV for institutions; foundational for colonial legacy literature.

ev-ir-waltz.title: Theory of International Politics
ev-ir-waltz.strength: The foundational structural realist text; Wikipedia article covers Waltz's anarchy-structure argument.

ev-ir-keohane.title: After Hegemony: Cooperation and Discord in the World Political Economy
ev-ir-keohane.strength: Founding text of neoliberal institutionalism — Wikipedia article covers international regimes and cooperation theory.

ev-ir-wendt.title: Social Theory of International Politics
ev-ir-wendt.strength: The foundational constructivist IR text; Wikipedia article covers norms, identity, and social construction.

ev-ir-liberal.title: Liberal international relations theory

ev-pe-political-business-cycle.title: Political business cycle

ev-pe-varieties-capitalism.title: Varieties of Capitalism: The Institutional Foundations of Comparative Advantage
ev-pe-varieties-capitalism.strength: Foundational text; Wikipedia covers LME vs CME distinction and comparative institutional advantage.

ev-pe-washington-consensus.title: Washington Consensus

ev-pe-social-contract.title: Social contract
ev-pe-social-contract.strength: Wikipedia article on Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau, and Rawls's contractarian tradition.

ev-socio-durkheim.title: The Rules of Sociological Method
ev-socio-durkheim.strength: Founding text of scientific sociology; Wikipedia article covers social facts, suicide, and division of labour.

ev-socio-weber.title: Economy and Society
ev-socio-weber.strength: Foundational sociological text; Wikipedia covers Weber's ideal types, verstehen, bureaucracy, and rationalization.

ev-socio-marx.title: Capital, Volume I
ev-socio-marx.strength: Primary text; Wikipedia covers base/superstructure, class conflict, and surplus value.

ev-socio-social-capital.title: Bowling Alone: The Collapse and Revival of American Community
ev-socio-social-capital.strength: Leading empirical study of social capital decline; Wikipedia article covers Bourdieu, Coleman, and Putnam's frameworks.

ev-socio-bourdieu.title: Distinction: A Social Critique of the Judgement of Taste
ev-socio-bourdieu.strength: Most cited sociology text of the 20th century (ISA); Wikipedia covers habitus, field, capital, and distinction.

ev-socio-stratification.title: Social stratification
ev-socio-stratification.strength: Wikipedia article on social stratification, class systems, and mobility.

ev-socio-anomie.title: Suicide: A Study in Sociology
ev-socio-anomie.strength: Foundational empirical sociology; Wikipedia article covers anomie and Merton's strain theory.

ev-socio-race.title: Race (sociology)
ev-socio-race.strength: Wikipedia article on race as social construction, systemic racism, and intersectionality.

ev-socio-goffman.title: The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life
ev-socio-goffman.strength: Foundational microsociology text; Wikipedia covers dramaturgy, stigma, and interaction order.

ev-socio-foucault-power.title: Discipline and Punish
ev-socio-foucault-power.strength: Highly influential; Wikipedia covers Foucault's concepts of power/knowledge, biopolitics, and discourse.

ev-socio-urbanisation.title: Urbanization

ev-socio-network.title: Social network
